title.zh: 卷五十五 列傳第五: 薛舉 李軌 劉武周 高開道 劉黑闥
title.en: Volume 55 Biographies 5: Xue Ju, Li Gui, Li Wuzhou,Gao Kaidao, Liu Heita
title.raw: 卷五十五 列傳第五: 薛舉 李軌 劉武周 高開道 劉黑闥 Volume 55 Biographies 5: Xue Ju, Li Gui, Li Wuzhou,Gao Kaidao, Liu Heita

sentences.zh: 薛舉，河東汾陰人也。

translations.literal: Xue Ju was a native of Fenyin in Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: Xue Ju came from Fenyin in Hedong.

sentences.zh: 其父汪，徙居金城。

translations.literal: His father Wang moved the family to Jincheng.
translations.idiomatic: His father Wang had relocated the household to Jincheng.

sentences.zh: 舉容貌瑰偉，凶悍善射，驍武絕倫，家產巨萬，交結豪猾，雄於邊朔。

translations.literal: Ju had a magnificent appearance, was fierce and skilled at archery, unmatched in martial valor, with family wealth in the tens of millions; he associated with powerful ruffians and was foremost on the northern frontier.
translations.idiomatic: Ju was striking in bearing, fierce, and an expert archer, with martial prowess beyond compare. His household possessed vast wealth, he cultivated ties with powerful local strongmen, and he dominated the northern marches.

sentences.zh: 初，為金城府校尉。

translations.literal: At first he served as a company commander in the Jincheng prefectural guard.
translations.idiomatic: He began his career as a company commander in the Jincheng prefectural guard.

sentences.zh: 大業末，隴西群盜蜂起，百姓飢餒，金城令郝瑗，募得數千人，使舉討捕。

translations.literal: At the end of the Daye era bandits rose throughout Longxi, the people were starving, and Jincheng Magistrate Hao Yuan raised several thousand men and sent Ju to pursue and suppress them.
translations.idiomatic: Late in the Daye reign, bandit armies swarmed across Longxi and the people faced famine. Jincheng Magistrate Hao Yuan recruited several thousand men and put Ju in command to hunt the raiders down.

sentences.zh: 授甲於郡中，吏人咸集，置酒以饗士。

translations.literal: Armor was issued in the commandery; officials and clerks all assembled, and wine was set out to feast the troops.
translations.idiomatic: When armor was issued in the commandery, officials and clerks alike gathered, and a feast was laid out for the soldiers.

sentences.zh: 舉與其子仁杲及同謀者十三人，於座中劫瑗，矯稱收捕反者，因發兵囚郡縣官，開倉以賑貧乏。

translations.literal: Ju, his son Rengao, and thirteen co-conspirators seized Yuan at the feast, falsely announcing that they were arresting rebels; they then raised troops, imprisoned the commandery and county officials, and opened the granaries to relieve the poor.
translations.idiomatic: At the banquet Ju, his son Rengao, and thirteen confederates seized Yuan, claiming they were rounding up rebels. They mobilized troops, imprisoned the commandery and county officials, and opened the granaries to feed the destitute.

sentences.zh: 自稱西秦霸王，建元為秦興，封仁杲為齊公，少子仁越為晉公。

translations.literal: He styled himself Overlord of Western Qin, adopted the era name Qin Xing, enfeoffed Rengao as Duke of Qi, and his younger son Renyue as Duke of Jin.
translations.idiomatic: He proclaimed himself Overlord of Western Qin, adopted the era name Qin Xing, made Rengao Duke of Qi, and his younger son Renyue Duke of Jin.

sentences.zh: 有宗羅睺者，先聚黨為群盜，至是帥眾會之，封為義興公，餘皆以次封拜。

translations.literal: There was one Zong Luohou who had earlier gathered a band of brigands; he now led his followers to join Ju and was enfeoffed as Duke of Yixing, while the rest received titles in due order.
translations.idiomatic: A brigand chief named Zong Luohou, who had long led a band of raiders, now brought his followers to Ju's banner. Ju enfeoffed him as Duke of Yixing and granted ranks to the others in turn.

sentences.zh: 掠官收馬，招集群盜，兵鋒甚銳，所至皆下。

translations.literal: He seized official stock and gathered horses, recruited bandits everywhere, and his army's edge was so keen that wherever it went, places submitted.
translations.idiomatic: He seized government herds, rounded up horses, and recruited bandits from every quarter. His army struck with devastating force, and every place he reached fell to him.

sentences.zh: 隋將皇甫綰屯兵一萬在枹罕，舉選精銳二千人襲之，與綰軍遇於赤岸，陳兵未戰，俄而風雨暴至。

translations.literal: The Sui general Huangfu Wan held ten thousand men at Fuhan; Ju chose two thousand elite troops to strike him. When the armies met at Chian, the formations were drawn up but battle had not yet begun when suddenly a violent storm broke.
translations.idiomatic: Sui general Huangfu Wan had ten thousand men encamped at Fuhan. Ju selected two thousand crack troops for a surprise attack. The armies met at Chian and had just formed for battle when a violent storm burst upon them.

sentences.zh: 初，風逆舉陣，而綰不擊之；

translations.literal: At first the wind blew against Ju's array, but Wan did not attack;
translations.idiomatic: At first the wind blew straight into Ju's ranks, yet Wan held his attack;

sentences.zh: 忽返風，正逆綰陣，氣色昏昧，軍中擾亂。

translations.literal: suddenly the wind shifted and blew straight into Wan's formation; the sky grew dim, and his army fell into disorder.
translations.idiomatic: then the wind swung around and drove full into Wan's line. The sky darkened and his troops fell into chaos.

sentences.zh: 舉策馬先登，眾軍從之，隋軍大潰，遂陷枹罕。

translations.literal: Ju spurred his horse to charge first; the whole army followed, the Sui forces were utterly routed, and Fuhan was taken.
translations.idiomatic: Ju spurred ahead at the head of the charge, his whole army surging after him. The Sui army collapsed in rout, and Fuhan fell.

sentences.zh: 時羌首鐘利俗擁兵二萬在岷山界，盡以眾降舉，兵遂大振。

translations.literal: At that time the Qiang leader Zhong Lisu held twenty thousand men on the Minshan frontier; he surrendered his entire force to Ju, and the army's strength surged.
translations.idiomatic: The Qiang chieftain Zhong Lisu then held twenty thousand men along the Minshan border. He surrendered his entire following to Ju, and Ju's power swelled dramatically.

sentences.zh: 進仁杲為齊王，授東道行軍元帥；

translations.literal: Rengao was advanced to Prince of Qi and appointed commander-in-chief of the eastern campaign;
translations.idiomatic: Rengao was elevated to Prince of Qi and named commander-in-chief of the eastern campaign;

sentences.zh: 仁越為晉王，兼河州刺史；

translations.literal: Renyue was made Prince of Jin and concurrently Governor of Hezhou;
translations.idiomatic: Renyue became Prince of Jin and concurrently Governor of Hezhou;

sentences.zh: 羅睺為義興王，以副仁杲。

translations.literal: Luohou was made Prince of Yixing to assist Rengao.
translations.idiomatic: Luohou was made Prince of Yixing to serve as Rengao's second-in-command.

sentences.zh: 總兵略地，又克鄯、廓二州，數日間，盡有隴西之地，眾至十三萬。

translations.literal: Concentrating his forces to seize territory, he also took Shan and Kuo prefectures; within a few days he held all of Longxi, and his followers reached one hundred thirty thousand.
translations.idiomatic: He marched at the head of his armies to seize territory, capturing Shan and Kuo prefectures as well. Within days he controlled all of Longxi, and his forces grew to one hundred thirty thousand.

sentences.zh: 十三年秋七月，舉僭號於蘭州，以妻鞠氏為皇后，母為皇太后，起墳塋，置陵邑，立廟於城南。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of autumn in the thirteenth year he usurped the imperial title at Lanzhou, made his wife Lady Qu empress, his mother empress dowager, raised tombs, established a mausoleum district, and built a temple south of the city.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of autumn in his thirteenth regnal year he declared himself emperor at Lanzhou. He made his wife, Lady Qu, empress and his mother empress dowager, laid out imperial tombs with a mausoleum district, and built a ancestral temple south of the city.

sentences.zh: 其月，舉陳兵數萬，出拜墓，禮畢大會。

translations.literal: That same month Ju arrayed tens of thousands of troops, went out to pay homage at the tombs, and when the rites were finished held a great assembly.
translations.idiomatic: That month he paraded tens of thousands of troops to the tombs for the rites of homage, then held a grand assembly when the ceremony was done.

sentences.zh: 仁杲進兵圍秦州。

translations.literal: Rengao advanced and besieged Qinzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Rengao marched forward and laid siege to Qinzhou.

sentences.zh: 仁越兵趨劍口，至河池郡，太守蕭瑀拒退之。

translations.literal: Renyue's force pressed toward Jiankou, reached Hechi Commandery, and was repelled by Prefect Xiao Yu.
translations.idiomatic: Renyue drove toward Jiankou and reached Hechi Commandery, where Prefect Xiao Yu beat his army back.

sentences.zh: 舉命其將常仲興渡河擊李軌，與軌將李贇大戰於昌松，仲興敗績，全軍陷於軌。

translations.literal: Ju ordered his general Chang Zhongxing to cross the river and attack Li Gui; he fought a great battle with Gui's general Li Yun at Changsong, Zhongxing was utterly defeated, and his entire army fell into Gui's hands.
translations.idiomatic: Ju sent his general Chang Zhongxing across the river to strike Li Gui. At Changsong he fought Gui's general Li Yun and suffered a crushing defeat; his whole army was lost to Gui.

sentences.zh: 及仁杲克秦州，舉自蘭州遷都之。

translations.literal: When Rengao took Qinzhou, Ju moved his capital there from Lanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: After Rengao captured Qinzhou, Ju moved his capital there from Lanzhou.

sentences.zh: 遣仁杲引軍寇扶風郡，汧源賊帥唐弼率眾拒之，兵不得進。

translations.literal: He sent Rengao to lead troops against Fufeng Commandery; the Qianyuan bandit chief Tang Bing gathered his followers to resist, and the army could not advance.
translations.idiomatic: He dispatched Rengao to raid Fufeng Commandery, but the Qianyuan bandit chief Tang Bing rallied his men to block the advance, and the army could not get through.

sentences.zh: 初，弼起扶風，立隴西李弘芝為天子，有徒十萬。

translations.literal: Earlier Bing had risen in Fufeng, set up Li Hongzhi of Longxi as Son of Heaven, and had a following of one hundred thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Bing had first risen in Fufeng, enthroned Li Hongzhi of Longxi as emperor, and gathered a host of one hundred thousand.

sentences.zh: 舉遣使招弼，弼殺弘芝，引軍從舉。

translations.literal: Ju sent envoys to win Bing over; Bing killed Hongzhi and led his army to join Ju.
translations.idiomatic: Ju sent envoys to recruit Bing, who killed Hongzhi and marched his forces to Ju's side.

sentences.zh: 仁杲因弼弛備，襲破之，並有其眾，弼以數百騎遁免。

translations.literal: Rengao, taking advantage of Bing's relaxed guard, struck and broke him, absorbing his whole force; Bing escaped with only a few hundred horsemen.
translations.idiomatic: While Bing's guard was down, Rengao ambushed and shattered him, absorbing his entire force. Bing fled with only a few hundred horsemen.

sentences.zh: 舉勢益張，軍號三十萬，將圖京師。

translations.literal: Ju's power grew still greater; his army was said to number three hundred thousand, and he planned to strike for the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Ju's power swelled further. His army was said to number three hundred thousand, and he set his sights on the capital.

sentences.zh: 會義兵定關中，遂留攻扶風。

translations.literal: Just then the righteous armies secured Guanzhong, so he remained to press the attack on Fufeng.
translations.idiomatic: But the loyalist armies were then securing Guanzhong, so he stayed behind to keep hammering at Fufeng.

sentences.zh: 太宗帥師討敗之，斬首數千級，追奔至隴坻而還。

translations.literal: Taizong led troops to defeat him, taking several thousand heads, pursued the rout to Longqi, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong led an army against him, routed his forces, and took several thousand heads. He chased the fugitives to Longqi before turning back.

sentences.zh: 舉又懼太宗逾隴追之，乃問其眾曰：「古來天子有降事否？」

translations.literal: Ju again feared that Taizong would cross Long to pursue him, and asked his followers, "In antiquity has any Son of Heaven ever submitted?"
translations.idiomatic: Ju now feared Taizong would cross the Long Mountains in pursuit and asked his followers, "Has any emperor in history ever surrendered?"

sentences.zh: 偽黃門侍郎褚亮曰：「昔越帝趙佗卒歸漢祖，蜀主劉禪亦仕晉朝，近代蕭琮，至今猶貴。

translations.literal: The false Household Attendant Chu Liang said, "In the past the Yue emperor Zhao Tuo in the end submitted to the Han Founder; the Shu ruler Liu Shan also served the Jin; in recent times Xiao Cong remains honored to this day.
translations.idiomatic: His false Household Attendant Chu Liang replied, "The Yue emperor Zhao Tuo eventually submitted to the Han founder; Liu Shan of Shu served the Jin; and in our own day Xiao Cong still enjoys high standing.

sentences.zh: 轉禍為福，自古有之。」

translations.literal: Turning calamity into blessing is something found in every age."
translations.idiomatic: Turning disaster into fortune is an old story."

sentences.zh: 其衛尉卿郝瑗趨而進曰：「皇帝失問。

translations.literal: His Commandant of the Guards Hao Yuan hurried forward and said, "Your Majesty has asked amiss.
translations.idiomatic: His Commandant of the Guards Hao Yuan stepped forward urgently and said, "Your Majesty has asked the wrong question.

sentences.zh: 褚亮之言，又何悖也！

translations.literal: How perverse are Chu Liang's words!
translations.idiomatic: Chu Liang's counsel is perverse!

sentences.zh: 昔漢祖屢經敗績，蜀先主亟亡妻子，戰之利害，何代無之？

translations.literal: In the past the Han Founder suffered defeat again and again; the Shu founder repeatedly lost wife and children—what age has been without the fortunes and misfortunes of war?
translations.idiomatic: The Han founder suffered defeat after defeat; the founder of Shu repeatedly lost wife and children. What age has been spared the swings of war?

sentences.zh: 安得一戰不捷，而為亡國之計也！」

translations.literal: How can one setback in battle justify plotting the ruin of a state!"
translations.idiomatic: How can a single lost battle justify talk of surrendering a kingdom!"

sentences.zh: 舉亦悔之，答曰：「聊發此問，試君等耳。」

translations.literal: Ju too regretted it and answered, "I raised this question only to test you all."
translations.idiomatic: Ju regretted the question as well and said, "I asked only to test you."

sentences.zh: 乃厚賞瑗，引為謀主。

translations.literal: He then richly rewarded Yuan and took him as chief strategist.
translations.idiomatic: He richly rewarded Yuan and made him his chief strategist.

sentences.zh: 瑗又勸舉連結梁師都，共為聲勢，厚賂突厥，餌其戎馬，合從併力，進逼京師。

translations.literal: Yuan further urged Ju to ally with Liang Shidu and make a joint show of force, bribe the Turks heavily and feed their war-horses, combine in alliance and united strength, and press on the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan urged Ju to ally with Liang Shidu for mutual support, lavish bribes on the Turks to secure their cavalry, join forces in alliance, and drive on the capital.

sentences.zh: 舉從其言，與突厥莫賀咄設謀取京師。

translations.literal: Ju followed his advice and plotted with the Turkic Moheduo she to seize the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Ju took his counsel and plotted with the Turkic leader Moheduo she to take the capital.

sentences.zh: 莫賀咄設許以兵隨之，期有日矣。

translations.literal: Moheduo she promised to follow with troops, and a date was set.
translations.idiomatic: Moheduo she promised troops would follow, and a day was fixed for the move.

sentences.zh: 會都水監宇文歆使於突厥，歆說莫賀咄設，止其出兵，故舉謀不行。

translations.literal: Just then Director of the Directorate of Waterways Yuwen Xin was envoy to the Turks; Xin persuaded Moheduo she to halt his march, and so Ju's plan came to nothing.
translations.idiomatic: At that moment Yuwen Xin of the Directorate of Waterways was on mission to the Turks and persuaded Moheduo she to hold back his army, so Ju's scheme came to nothing.

sentences.zh: 武德元年，豐州總管張長遜進擊宗羅睺，舉悉眾來援，軍屯高墌，縱兵虜掠，至於豳、岐之地。

translations.literal: In the first year of Wude, Fengzhou Commander-in-Chief Zhang Changsun advanced against Zong Luohou; Ju brought his entire force to the rescue, encamped at Gaoping, and let his troops raid and plunder as far as Bin and Qi.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Wude, Fengzhou commander Zhang Changsun attacked Zong Luohou. Ju marched out with his whole army to relieve him, encamped at Gaoping, and unleashed raiders across Bin and Qi.

sentences.zh: 太宗又率眾擊之，軍次高墌城，度其糧少，意在速戰，乃命深溝堅壁，以老其師。

translations.literal: Taizong again led troops against him, halting at Gaoping city; judging that the enemy had little grain and wanted a quick battle, he ordered deep trenches and stout walls to wear down their army.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong marched out again and halted at Gaoping. Seeing that the enemy was short of grain and eager for a quick fight, he ordered deep entrenchments and strong walls to wear them down.

sentences.zh: 未及與戰，會太宗不豫，行軍長史劉文靜、殷開山請觀兵於高墌西南，恃眾不設備，為舉兵掩乘其後。

translations.literal: Before battle was joined Taizong fell ill; the campaign chief clerk Liu Wenjing and Yin Kaishan asked to review the troops southwest of Gaoping, trusting in their numbers and taking no precautions, and were overrun from the rear by Ju's army.
translations.idiomatic: Before battle could be joined Taizong fell ill. Campaign chief clerk Liu Wenjing and Yin Kaishan asked to inspect the troops southwest of Gaoping. Confident in their numbers, they took no precautions, and Ju's army fell on them from behind.

sentences.zh: 太宗聞之，知其必敗，遽與書責之。

translations.literal: When Taizong heard of it he knew they would be defeated and hurriedly sent a letter rebuking them.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing of this, Taizong knew disaster was coming and sent an urgent letter of rebuke.

sentences.zh: 未至，兩軍合戰，竟為舉所敗，死者十五六，大將慕容羅睺、李安遠、劉弘基皆陷於陣。

translations.literal: Before it arrived the two armies had joined battle and were utterly defeated by Ju; fifteen or sixteen out of every hundred were killed, and the great generals Murong Luohou, Li Anyuan, and Liu Hongji all fell in the field.
translations.idiomatic: The letter had not yet arrived when the armies clashed and were routed by Ju. Fifteen or sixteen men in every hundred were killed, and the great generals Murong Luohou, Li Anyuan, and Liu Hongji were all captured in the battle.

sentences.zh: 太宗歸於京師，舉軍取高墌，又遣仁杲進圍寧州。

translations.literal: Taizong returned to the capital; Ju's army took Gaoping and again sent Rengao forward to besiege Ningzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong withdrew to the capital. Ju seized Gaoping and sent Rengao on to besiege Ningzhou.

sentences.zh: 郝瑗言於舉曰：「今唐兵新破，將帥並擒，京師騷動，可乘勝直取長安。」

translations.literal: Hao Yuan said to Ju, "Now the Tang army has just been broken, its commanders all captured, and the capital is in turmoil—you can seize the moment and drive straight for Chang'an."
translations.idiomatic: Hao Yuan told Ju, "The Tang army has just been shattered, its commanders taken, and the capital is in uproar. You can strike while victory is hot and march straight on Chang'an."

sentences.zh: 舉然之。

translations.literal: Ju agreed.
translations.idiomatic: Ju agreed.

sentences.zh: 臨發而舉疾，召巫視之，巫言唐兵為祟，舉惡之，未幾而死。

translations.literal: Just as he was about to march Ju fell ill; he summoned a shaman to divine the cause, and the shaman said the Tang army was haunting him. Ju took this ill and soon died.
translations.idiomatic: On the eve of departure Ju fell ill. A shaman he summoned declared that Tang spirits were tormenting him. Ju took the omen badly and died not long after.

sentences.zh: 舉每破陣，所獲士卒皆殺之，殺人多斷舌、割鼻，或碓搗之。

translations.literal: Whenever Ju broke an enemy formation he killed every soldier taken; many he killed by cutting out the tongue or slicing off the nose, or pounding them in a mortar.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever Ju broke an enemy line he slaughtered every captive. Many he killed by cutting out their tongues or slicing off their noses, or pounding them in a mortar.

sentences.zh: 其妻性又酷暴，好鞭撻其下，見人不勝痛而宛轉於地，則埋其足，才露腹背而捶之。

translations.literal: His wife was likewise cruel and violent, fond of flogging her subordinates; when she saw someone writhing on the ground from pain she would bury his feet and beat only the belly and back that showed above.
translations.idiomatic: His wife was equally brutal, delighting in flogging subordinates. When a victim writhed on the ground in agony she would bury his feet and beat only the belly and back left exposed.

sentences.zh: 由是人心不附。

translations.literal: Because of this men's hearts did not attach to them.
translations.idiomatic: For this reason their followers' loyalty waned.

sentences.zh: 仁杲代董其眾，偽謚舉為武皇帝，未葬而仁杲滅。

translations.literal: Rengao succeeded him in command of the host, gave Ju the false posthumous title Martial Emperor, and before the burial was complete Rengao was destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: Rengao took command of his forces, gave Ju the posthumous title Martial Emperor, and was destroyed before the funeral rites were finished.

translations.literal: 〈Son〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈His son〉

sentences.zh: 薛仁杲

translations.literal: Xue Rengao
translations.idiomatic: Xue Rengao

sentences.zh: 仁杲，舉長子也，多力善騎射，軍中號為萬人敵。

translations.literal: Rengao was Ju's eldest son, possessed of great strength and skilled in mounted archery; in the army he was called a match for ten thousand men.
translations.idiomatic: Rengao, Ju's eldest son, was immensely strong and a master of mounted archery. The army called him a match for ten thousand men.

sentences.zh: 然所至多殺人，納其妻妾。

translations.literal: Yet wherever he went he killed many and took their wives and concubines.
translations.idiomatic: Wherever he marched he slaughtered freely and seized men's wives and concubines.

sentences.zh: 獲庾信子立，怒其不降，磔於猛火之上，漸割以啖軍士。

translations.literal: He captured Li, son of Yu Xin, and in anger at his refusal to submit dismembered him over a fierce fire, cutting him piece by piece to feed the soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: He captured Li, son of the poet Yu Xin, and enraged by his refusal to submit had him dismembered over a roaring fire, cutting flesh piece by piece to feed the troops.

sentences.zh: 初，拔秦州，悉召富人倒懸之，以醋灌鼻，或杙其下竅，以求金寶。

translations.literal: When he first took Qinzhou he summoned all the wealthy, hung them upside down, poured vinegar into their nostrils, or drove stakes through their lower orifices to extort gold and jewels.
translations.idiomatic: When he first seized Qinzhou he rounded up the wealthy, hung them head down, poured vinegar into their nostrils, or drove stakes through their lower bodies to wring out gold and jewels.

sentences.zh: 舉每誡之曰：「汝智略縱橫，足辦我家事，而傷於苛虐，與物無恩，終當覆我宗社。」

translations.literal: Ju often admonished him, saying, "Your stratagems are far-ranging and quite enough to manage our house's affairs, but you are harmed by harsh cruelty and show no kindness to others—you will in the end overturn our clan and state."
translations.idiomatic: Ju often warned him, "Your schemes are resourceful enough to carry our house, but your cruelty and want of mercy toward others will in the end destroy our line and our kingdom."

sentences.zh: 舉死，仁杲立於折墌城，與諸將帥素多有隙，及嗣位，眾咸猜懼。

translations.literal: When Ju died Rengao established himself at Zheyuancheng; he had long had many rifts with the various generals, and when he succeeded to power all were suspicious and afraid.
translations.idiomatic: After Ju's death Rengao held court at Zheyuancheng. He had long been at odds with many of his generals, and when he took the throne his followers were rife with suspicion and fear.

sentences.zh: 郝瑗哭舉悲思，因病不起，自此兵勢日衰。

translations.literal: Hao Yuan wept for Ju in grief and took to his bed with illness; from this time their military strength daily declined.
translations.idiomatic: Hao Yuan mourned Ju in grief until illness laid him low, and from that day their military strength steadily waned.

sentences.zh: 自劉文靜為舉所敗後，高祖命太宗率諸軍以擊仁杲，師次高墌，而堅壁不動。

translations.literal: After Liu Wenjing was defeated by Ju, Gaozu ordered Taizong to lead the armies against Rengao; the army halted at Gaoping and held fast behind walls without moving.
translations.idiomatic: After Liu Wenjing's defeat by Ju, Gaozu ordered Taizong to lead the armies against Rengao. The army halted at Gaoping and held behind stout walls without giving battle.

sentences.zh: 諸將咸請戰，太宗曰：「我士卒新敗，銳氣猶少。

translations.literal: The generals all asked to give battle; Taizong said, "Our soldiers have just been defeated and their fighting spirit is still low.
translations.idiomatic: The generals all pressed for battle. Taizong said, "Our men have just suffered defeat and their fighting spirit is still low.

sentences.zh: 賊以勝自驕，必輕敵好鬥，故且閉壁以折之。

translations.literal: The rebels, flushed with victory, will surely despise the enemy and be eager to fight; therefore for now we close the walls to break their ardor.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels are drunk on victory and will surely grow reckless and eager to fight. For now we hold the walls to break their spirit.

sentences.zh: 待其氣衰而後奮擊，可一戰而破，此萬全計也。」

translations.literal: When their spirit has waned we will strike hard and can break them in a single battle—this is the plan of perfect safety."
translations.idiomatic: When their ardor fades we will strike with full force and break them in one battle. That is the sure plan."

sentences.zh: 乃令軍中曰：「敢言戰者斬。」

translations.literal: He then ordered the army, "Whoever dares speak of giving battle shall be beheaded."
translations.idiomatic: He then proclaimed through the army, "Anyone who speaks of giving battle will be beheaded."

sentences.zh: 相持者久之。

translations.literal: The standoff lasted a long while.
translations.idiomatic: The stalemate dragged on for a long time.

sentences.zh: 仁杲勇而無謀，兼糧饋不屬，將士稍離，其內史令翟長孫以其眾來降，仁杲妹夫偽左僕射鐘俱仇以河州歸國。

translations.literal: Rengao was brave but without strategy; moreover supplies failed to reach him and officers and soldiers gradually deserted. His Director of the Imperial Secretariat Zhai Zhangsun came over with his followers, and Rengao's brother-in-law the false Left Vice Director Zhong Juqiu surrendered Hezhou to the Tang.
translations.idiomatic: Rengao was bold but lacked strategy, supplies failed to reach him, and his officers and men began to slip away. His Director of the Imperial Secretariat Zhai Zhangsun defected with his troops, and Rengao's brother-in-law, the false Left Vice Director Zhong Juqiu, surrendered Hezhou to the Tang.

sentences.zh: 太宗知其可擊，遣將軍龐玉擊賊將宗羅睺於淺水原。

translations.literal: Taizong knew the moment had come to strike and sent General Pang Yu to attack the rebel general Zong Luohou at Qianshuiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing the moment ripe, Taizong sent General Pang Yu to strike the rebel general Zong Luohou at Qianshuiyuan.

sentences.zh: 兩軍酣戰，太宗以勁兵出賊不意，奮擊大破之。

translations.literal: The two armies fought fiercely; Taizong brought elite troops against the enemy's blind side and struck with full force, routing them utterly.
translations.idiomatic: As the two armies grappled in fierce combat, Taizong led elite troops in an unexpected thrust and shattered the enemy line.

sentences.zh: 乘勝進薄其折墌城，仁杲窮蹙，率偽百官開門降，太宗納之。

translations.literal: Pressing the victory he advanced on Zheyuancheng; Rengao, driven to extremity, led his false court officials to open the gates and submit, and Taizong accepted the surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Pressing the victory he advanced on Zheyuancheng. Cornered, Rengao led his false court out to open the gates in surrender, and Taizong accepted.

sentences.zh: 王師振旅，以仁杲歸於京師，及其首帥數十人皆斬之。

translations.literal: The royal army returned in triumph, bringing Rengao to the capital, and several tens of his chieftains were all beheaded.
translations.idiomatic: The imperial army marched home in triumph with Rengao to the capital, and several dozen of his chieftains were beheaded.

sentences.zh: 舉父子相繼偽位至滅，凡五年，隴西平。

translations.literal: Ju and his son in succession held the false throne until their destruction—altogether five years—and Longxi was pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Father and son had held the false throne in succession until their destruction, a span of five years in all, and Longxi was pacified.

sentences.zh: 李軌，字處則，武威姑臧人也。

translations.literal: Li Gui, styled Chuze, was a native of Guzang in Wuwei.
translations.idiomatic: Li Gui, whose courtesy name was Chuze, came from Guzang in Wuwei.

sentences.zh: 有機辯，頗窺書籍，家富於財，賑窮濟乏，人亦稱之。

translations.literal: He was quick-witted and eloquent, had dipped into books, his household was rich in wealth, and he relieved the poor and aided the destitute—men praised him for this as well.
translations.idiomatic: Quick-witted and articulate, he had some learning from books. His household was wealthy, and he was known for relieving the poor and aiding the needy, which won him praise.

sentences.zh: 大業末，為鷹揚府司馬。

translations.literal: At the end of the Daye era he served as military aide in the Eagle-Flying Guard.
translations.idiomatic: Late in the Daye reign he served as military aide in the Eagle-Flying Guard.

sentences.zh: 時薛舉作亂於金城，軌與同郡曹珍、關謹、梁碩、李贇、安修仁等謀曰：「薛舉殘暴，必來侵擾，郡官庸怯，無以御之。

translations.literal: At that time Xue Ju was in rebellion at Jincheng; Gui plotted with his fellow countrymen Cao Zhen, Guan Jin, Liang Shuo, Li Yun, An Xiuren, and others, saying, "Xue Ju is brutal and will surely come to raid us; the commandery officials are mediocre and timid and cannot defend against him.
translations.idiomatic: When Xue Ju rose in rebellion at Jincheng, Gui met with his countrymen Cao Zhen, Guan Jin, Liang Shuo, Li Yun, An Xiuren, and others and said, "Xue Ju is brutal and will surely raid us. The commandery officials are timid and incompetent and cannot hold him off.

sentences.zh: 今宜同心戮力，保據河右，以觀天下之事，豈可束手於人，妻子分散！」

translations.literal: Now we ought to join hearts and combine strength, hold the lands west of the Yellow River, and watch how affairs in the empire unfold—how can we sit bound hand and foot while wives and children are scattered!"
translations.idiomatic: We should unite in purpose, hold the lands west of the Yellow River, and watch how the empire unfolds. How can we sit idle while our wives and children are torn apart!"

sentences.zh: 乃謀共舉兵，皆相讓，莫肯為主。

translations.literal: They then plotted to raise troops together, but each deferred to the others and none would be leader.
translations.idiomatic: They resolved to raise troops together, yet each deferred to the others and none would take command.

sentences.zh: 曹珍曰：「常聞圖讖云『李氏當王』。

translations.literal: Cao Zhen said, "I have often heard prophetic texts say, 'The house of Li shall reign.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Zhen said, "I have often heard prophetic texts declare, 'The house of Li shall reign.

sentences.zh: 今軌在謀中，豈非天命也？」

translations.literal: Now Gui is among our plotters—is this not Heaven's mandate?"
translations.idiomatic: Gui stands among us in this plot—is that not Heaven's mandate?"

sentences.zh: 遂拜賀之，推以為主。

translations.literal: They then bowed in congratulation and pushed him forward as leader.
translations.idiomatic: They bowed in congratulation and pressed him to lead.

sentences.zh: 軌令修仁夜率諸胡入內苑城，建旗大呼，軌於郭下聚眾應之，執縛隋虎賁郎將謝統師、郡丞韋士政。

translations.literal: Gui ordered Xiuren by night to lead the various non-Chinese into the Inner Garden city, raise banners and shout; Gui gathered followers outside the walls to answer them and seized the Sui Tiger-Gallant General Xie Tongshi and the commandery aide Wei Shizheng.
translations.idiomatic: Gui sent Xiuren by night to lead the frontier peoples into the Inner Garden city, raise banners, and raise the cry. Gui rallied followers outside the walls to join them and seized the Sui Tiger-Gallant General Xie Tongshi and commandery aide Wei Shizheng.

sentences.zh: 軌自稱河西大涼王，建元安樂，署置官屬，並擬開皇故事。

translations.literal: Gui styled himself Great King of Liang of Hexi, adopted the era name Anle, appointed officials, and modeled everything on Kaihuang precedents.
translations.idiomatic: Gui proclaimed himself Great King of Liang of Hexi, adopted the era name Anle, appointed a full bureaucracy, and modeled his court on Kaihuang precedents.

sentences.zh: 初，突厥曷娑那可汗率眾內屬，遣弟闕達度闕設領部落在會寧川中，有二千餘騎，至是自稱可汗，來降於軌。

translations.literal: Earlier the Turkic khan Tumen had led his people to submit to the interior and sent his younger brother Quedu du she to lead his tribes in the Huining valley with more than two thousand horsemen; they now styled themselves khans in their own right and came to submit to Gui.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier the Turkic khan Tumen had submitted with his people and sent his younger brother Quedu du she to camp with more than two thousand horsemen in the Huining valley. They now styled themselves khans in their own right and submitted to Gui.

sentences.zh: 其年，軌殺其吏部尚書梁碩。

translations.literal: That same year Gui killed his Director of the Ministry of Personnel Liang Shuo.
translations.idiomatic: That year Gui killed his Director of the Ministry of Personnel, Liang Shuo.

sentences.zh: 初，軌之起也，碩為謀主，甚有智略，眾咸憚之。

translations.literal: When Gui first rose, Shuo had been chief strategist, possessed of great wisdom and stratagem, and all feared him.
translations.idiomatic: When Gui first rose, Shuo had been his chief strategist, a man of keen intelligence whom everyone feared.

sentences.zh: 碩見諸胡種落繁盛，乃陰勸軌宜加防察，與其戶部尚書安修仁由是有隙。

translations.literal: Shuo saw that the various non-Chinese tribes were flourishing and secretly urged Gui to strengthen precautions and scrutiny; because of this he came into conflict with his Director of the Ministry of Revenue An Xiuren.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing the frontier tribes growing strong, Shuo secretly urged Gui to tighten his guard against them, and for this he fell out with his Director of the Ministry of Revenue, An Xiuren.

sentences.zh: 又軌子仲琰懷恨，形於辭色，修仁因之構成碩罪，更譖毀之，雲其欲反，軌令齎鴆就宅殺焉。

translations.literal: Moreover Gui's son Zhongyan harbored resentment that showed in word and countenance; Xiuren used this to fabricate charges against Shuo and further slandered him, saying he intended rebellion, and Gui ordered poison brought to his house to kill him.
translations.idiomatic: Gui's son Zhongyan also bore a grudge that showed plainly in his words and face. Xiuren used this to frame Shuo and spread further slander that he planned rebellion. Gui sent poison to Shuo's house and had him killed.

sentences.zh: 是後，故人多疑懼之，心膂從此稍離。

translations.literal: After this his old companions were full of suspicion and fear, and the hearts closest to him from this time gradually drew away.
translations.idiomatic: After this his old companions grew suspicious and afraid, and his closest supporters gradually drifted away.

sentences.zh: 時高祖方圖薛舉，遣使潛往涼州與之相結，下璽書，謂之為從弟。

translations.literal: At that time Gaozu was planning against Xue Ju and sent envoys secretly to Liangzhou to ally with him, issuing an imperial letter calling him younger cousin.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu was then planning his campaign against Xue Ju and sent secret envoys to Liangzhou to ally with Gui, issuing an imperial letter that addressed him as younger cousin.

sentences.zh: 軌大悅，遣其弟懋入朝，獻方物。

translations.literal: Gui was greatly pleased and sent his younger brother Mao to court with tribute goods.
translations.idiomatic: Gui was delighted and sent his younger brother Mao to court with local tribute.

sentences.zh: 高祖授懋大將軍，遣還涼州。

translations.literal: Gaozu appointed Mao Great General and sent him back to Liangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu appointed Mao Great General and sent him back to Liangzhou.

sentences.zh: 又令鴻臚少卿張侯德持節，冊拜為涼州總管，封涼王，給羽葆鼓吹一部。

translations.literal: He also ordered Vice Director of the Court of Diplomatic Reception Zhang Houde to bear the staff of office and invest him as Commander-in-Chief of Liangzhou, enfeoff him as King of Liang, and grant one set of feathered parasols and martial music.
translations.idiomatic: He also sent Vice Director of the Court of Diplomatic Reception Zhang Houde with credentials to invest Gui as Commander-in-Chief of Liangzhou, enfeoff him as King of Liang, and grant a full set of imperial parasols and martial music.

sentences.zh: 軌召群僚廷議曰：「今吾從兄膺受圖籙，據有京邑，天命可知，一姓不宜競立，今去帝號受冊可乎？」

translations.literal: Gui summoned the assembled officials to a court deliberation, saying: "Now my paternal cousin has received the Mandate in accordance with the celestial signs, holds the capital, and the will of Heaven is clear — one surname ought not vie for supremacy. Would it be acceptable now to relinquish the imperial title and accept an investiture?
translations.idiomatic: Li Gui summoned his ministers for a court debate. "My cousin has received Heaven's mandate and taken the capital," he said. "The signs are clear — two dynasties should not compete. Should we give up our imperial title and accept Tang investiture instead?

sentences.zh: 曹珍進曰：「隋失天下，英雄競逐，稱王號帝，鼎峙瓜分。

translations.literal: Cao Zhen stepped forward and said: "The Sui has lost the realm; heroes compete in the chase, proclaiming themselves kings and emperors, standing like tripods in rivalry and dividing the land.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Zhen stepped forward. "The Sui has lost the empire," he said. "Heroes are racing to seize it — kings and emperors spring up everywhere, each holding a piece of the realm like rival tripods dividing the land.

sentences.zh: 唐國自據關中，大涼自處河右，己為天子，奈何受人官爵？

translations.literal: The Tang state holds Guanzhong for itself, and Great Liang has its place in Hexi — we are already emperors. How can we accept offices and ranks from others?
translations.idiomatic: Tang holds Guanzhong; we hold Hexi as Great Liang. We are already emperors in our own right — why should we accept titles and offices from anyone else?

sentences.zh: 若欲以小事大，宜依蕭察故事，自稱梁帝而稱臣於周。」

translations.literal: If you wish to serve the greater power as the lesser, you should follow the precedent of Xiao Cha — style oneself Emperor of Liang while becoming a subject of Zhou."
translations.idiomatic: If you truly mean to serve the stronger power as the weaker one, follow the example of Xiao Cha: call yourself Emperor of Liang, but acknowledge Zhou as your sovereign."

sentences.zh: 軌從之。

translations.literal: Gui assented.
translations.idiomatic: Li Gui agreed.

sentences.zh: 二年，遣其尚書左丞鄧曉隨使者入朝，表稱皇從弟大涼皇帝臣軌而不受官。

translations.literal: In the second year, he sent his Minister of the Left of the Department of State Affairs, Deng Xiao, to accompany the envoy to court. In the memorial he styled himself the Tang emperor's imperial younger cousin, Emperor of Great Liang, and Subject Gui, but would not accept any office.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year he sent his Minister of the Left, Deng Xiao, to Chang'an with the Tang envoy. Deng's memorial addressed the Tang emperor as his imperial cousin and styled Li Gui "Emperor of Great Liang, your subject Gui" — but Li Gui refused to accept any Tang office.

sentences.zh: 時有胡巫惑之曰：「上帝當遣玉女從天而降。」

translations.literal: At the time a Hu shaman deluded him, saying: "Heaven's Lord will send a jade maiden to descend from the sky.
translations.idiomatic: A Hu shaman then deceived him, saying, "Heaven will send a jade maiden down from the sky.

sentences.zh: 遂徵兵築台以候玉女，多所糜費，百姓患之。

translations.literal: He then conscripted troops and built a platform to await the jade maiden — expenses were great, and the common people suffered from it.
translations.idiomatic: Li Gui conscripted labor and built a platform to await her. The project squandered vast sums, and the people groaned under the burden.

sentences.zh: 又屬年飢，人相食，軌傾家賑之，私家罄盡，不能周遍。

translations.literal: There was also a year of famine; people ate one another. Gui emptied his household to relieve them, but his private means were exhausted and he could not reach everyone.
translations.idiomatic: Famine followed. People ate one another. Li Gui poured out his family's wealth to feed the starving, but his private stores ran dry and he could not help everyone.

sentences.zh: 又欲開倉給粟，召眾議之。

translations.literal: He also wished to open the granaries and distribute grain, and summoned everyone to discuss it.
translations.idiomatic: He then proposed opening the state granaries and distributing grain, and called his advisers together to debate the idea.

sentences.zh: 珍等對曰：「國以人為本，本既不立，國將傾危，安可惜此倉粟，而坐觀百姓之死乎？」

translations.literal: Cao Zhen and the others replied: "The state takes the people as its foundation. If the foundation is not established, the state will topple into peril. How can we begrudge this granary grain and sit by watching the common people die?
translations.idiomatic: Cao Zhen and his allies replied, "A state lives or dies by its people. If the people collapse, the state collapses with them. How can we hoard this grain and watch the common folk starve?

sentences.zh: 其故人皆云，給粟為便。

translations.literal: His old associates all said that distributing grain would be the right course.
translations.idiomatic: Li Gui's old followers agreed that opening the granaries was the right move.

sentences.zh: 謝統師等隋舊官人，為軌所獲，雖被任使，情猶不附。

translations.literal: Xie Tongshi and other former Sui officials, whom Gui had taken in, though given duties, still did not feel attached in heart.
translations.idiomatic: Xie Tongshi and other former Sui officials whom Li Gui had captured and put to work still did not feel loyal to him at heart.

sentences.zh: 每與群胡相結，引進朋黨，排軌舊人，因其大餒，欲離其眾。

translations.literal: They constantly allied with the various Hu people, brought in their own factions, pushed aside Gui's old associates, and exploiting the great famine, sought to drive away his followers.
translations.idiomatic: They kept allying with the Hu factions, bringing in their own cliques and pushing aside Li Gui's old men. Exploiting the famine, they hoped to peel his followers away.

sentences.zh: 乃詬珍曰：「百姓餓者自是弱人，勇壯之士終不肯困，國家倉粟須備不虞，豈可散之以供小弱？

translations.literal: They then reviled Cao Zhen, saying: "Those among the common people who starve are naturally the weak. Bold and strong men would never accept such hardship. The state's granary grain must be kept for unforeseen need — how can we scatter it to feed the feeble?
translations.idiomatic: They attacked Cao Zhen directly. "The starving are the weak," they said. "Strong men will never go hungry. State grain must be kept for emergencies — why pour it out for the helpless?

sentences.zh: 僕射苟悅人情，殊非國計。」

translations.literal: The Minister Vice-President seeks only to please popular sentiment — this is utterly contrary to state policy.
translations.idiomatic: The Vice-President is pandering to the crowd. That is no way to run a state.

sentences.zh: 軌以為然，由是士庶怨憤，多欲叛之。

translations.literal: Gui thought this correct. Thereupon gentry and commoners grew resentful and angry, and many wished to rebel against him.
translations.idiomatic: Li Gui agreed with them. Gentry and commoners alike turned resentful, and many began looking for a way out.

sentences.zh: 初，安修仁之兄興貴先在長安，表請詣涼州招慰軌。

translations.literal: Earlier, An Xinggui, the elder brother of An Xiuren, had been in Chang'an and submitted a memorial requesting to go to Liangzhou to offer reassurance and win over Gui.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, An Xinggui — elder brother of An Xiuren — had been in Chang'an and petitioned to go to Liangzhou to win Li Gui over peacefully.

sentences.zh: 高祖謂曰：「李軌據河西之地，連好吐谷渾，結援於突厥，興兵討擊，尚以為難，豈單使所能致也？」

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozu said to him: "Li Gui holds the lands of Hexi, maintains friendly ties with Tuyuhun, and has secured aid from the Turks. To raise troops and attack would still be considered difficult — how could a lone envoy accomplish it?
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozu said to him, "Li Gui holds Hexi, keeps friendly ties with Tuyuhun, and has Turkic backing. Even a military campaign would be hard — how could one envoy alone bring him in?

sentences.zh: 興貴對曰：「李軌凶強，誠如聖旨。

translations.literal: Xinggui replied: "Li Gui is fierce and strong — it is indeed as Your Majesty says.
translations.idiomatic: Xinggui replied, "Li Gui is fierce and formidable — Your Majesty is right.

sentences.zh: 今若諭之以逆順，曉之以禍福，彼則憑固負遠，必不見從。

translations.literal: If we now instruct him in loyalty and rebellion and enlighten him in blessings and calamities, he will rely on his stronghold and distance and surely not follow.
translations.idiomatic: If we try to lecture him on loyalty and treason, blessings and ruin, he will hide behind his distance and his walls and never listen.

sentences.zh: 何則？

translations.literal: Why is this?
translations.idiomatic: Why?

sentences.zh: 臣於涼州，奕代豪望，凡厥士庶，靡不依附。

translations.literal: In Liangzhou I am a hereditary leader of great standing — among all gentry and commoners, none fails to attach themselves to me.
translations.idiomatic: In Liangzhou my family has been a leading house for generations. Gentry and commoners alike look to me.

sentences.zh: 臣之弟為軌所信任，職典樞密者數十人，以此候隙圖之，易於反掌，無不濟矣。」

translations.literal: My younger brother is trusted by Gui; there are several dozen men who handle the inner secrets of state. With this, to watch for an opening and plot against him would be as easy as turning one's palm — nothing would fail."
translations.idiomatic: My brother enjoys Li Gui's trust, and dozens of men around him hold the keys to state secrets. Wait for the right moment and strike — it would be as easy as turning my hand. It cannot fail."

sentences.zh: 高祖從之。

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozu agreed.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozu approved the plan.

sentences.zh: 興貴至涼州，軌授以左右衛大將軍，又問以自安之術，興貴諭之曰：「涼州僻遠，人物凋殘，勝兵雖余十萬，開地不過千里，既無險固，又接蕃戎，戎狄豺狼，非我族類，此而可久，實用為疑。

translations.literal: When Xinggui arrived at Liangzhou, Gui appointed him Grand General of the Left and Right Guards, and also asked him for a method of securing himself. Xinggui admonished him, saying: "Liangzhou is remote and isolated; its people are depleted and broken. Though fit soldiers remain above a hundred thousand, the territory opened does not exceed a thousand li. There are no strong defenses, and it borders the frontier barbarians. The barbarians are wolves — not our kind. That this could last long is truly doubtful.
translations.idiomatic: When Xinggui reached Liangzhou, Li Gui made him Grand General of the Left and Right Guards and asked how he might secure his position. Xinggui urged him, "Liangzhou is remote and its people are exhausted. You may have a hundred thousand soldiers left, but your domain stretches barely a thousand li. You have no natural defenses, and barbarian peoples press your borders — wolves who are not of our kind. How long can such a hold last? I have my doubts.

sentences.zh: 今大唐據有京邑，略定中原，攻必取，戰必勝，是天所啟，非人力焉。

translations.literal: Now Great Tang holds the capital, has largely settled the Central Plains — attack and it must be taken, battle and victory is sure. This is opened by Heaven, not human strength.
translations.idiomatic: Great Tang now holds the capital and has largely pacified the Central Plains. Its armies take what they attack and win every battle they fight. Heaven is opening the way — this is not mere human strength.

sentences.zh: 今若舉河西之地委質事之，即漢家竇融，未足為比。」

translations.literal: If you now offer up the lands west of the Yellow River and submit your allegiance, even Dou Rong of Han would not be worth comparison.
translations.idiomatic: Submit Hexi now and swear allegiance, and your reward will outshine even Dou Rong of the Han.

sentences.zh: 軌默然不答，久之，謂興貴曰：「昔吳濞以江左之兵，猶稱己為『東帝』；

translations.literal: Gui was silent and did not answer. After a long while he said to Xinggui: "In the past Wu Pi, with the armies of the lands east of the Yangtze, still styled himself 'Eastern Emperor';
translations.idiomatic: Li Gui said nothing for a long time. At last he told Xinggui, "In the old days Wu Pi commanded the armies of the lower Yangtze and still called himself the Eastern Emperor.

sentences.zh: 我今以河右之眾，豈得不為『西帝』？

translations.literal: With the masses of Hexi at my command today, how can I fail to be 'Western Emperor'?"
translations.idiomatic: With the armies of Hexi at my back, how can I not be the Western Emperor?"

sentences.zh: 彼雖強大，其如帝何？

translations.literal: Though they are powerful, what can they do to an emperor?
translations.idiomatic: However strong they are, what can they do to an emperor?

sentences.zh: 君與唐為計，誘引於我，酬彼恩遇耳。」

translations.literal: You scheme for Tang's sake, lure me with persuasion — that is repayment for their kindness to you."
translations.idiomatic: You are scheming for Tang, trying to lure me in — repayment for the favor they showed you."

sentences.zh: 興貴懼，乃偽謝曰：「竊聞富貴不在故鄉，有如衣錦夜行。

translations.literal: Xinggui was afraid, and so falsely apologized, saying: "I have heard that wealth and honor are not found in one's homeland — it is like wearing brocade and walking at night.
translations.idiomatic: Alarmed, Xinggui feigned remorse. "They say wealth and honor are not found in one's hometown," he said, "like wearing brocade and walking at night.

sentences.zh: 今合家子弟並蒙信任，榮慶實在一門，豈敢興心，更懷他志？」

translations.literal: Now my whole family and my younger kinsmen all enjoy his trust; glory rests in one household — how would I dare harbor another intent or cherish other designs?"
translations.idiomatic: My whole family now enjoys your trust; our honor rests in one house. How could I dare turn my heart elsewhere?"

sentences.zh: 興貴知軌不可動，乃與修仁等潛謀，引諸胡眾起兵圖軌，將圍其城，軌率步騎千餘出城拒戰。

translations.literal: Xinggui knew Gui could not be moved. He then secretly plotted with Xiuren and the others, rousing the various Hu peoples to raise troops against Gui. As they were about to surround the city, Gui led more than a thousand infantry and cavalry out to resist.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing that Li Gui would not budge, Xinggui secretly joined An Xiuren and the others to rouse the Hu factions in revolt. As they prepared to besiege the city, Li Gui led more than a thousand foot and horse soldiers out to fight.

sentences.zh: 先時，有薛舉柱國奚道宜，率羌兵三百人亡奔於軌，既許其刺史而不授之，禮遇又薄，深懷憤怨。

translations.literal: Earlier, there was Xi Daoyi, a pillar of state under Xue Ju, who led three hundred Qiang soldiers in flight to Gui. Gui had promised him a provincial governorship but never granted it, and his courtesy was also meager — Daoyi nursed deep resentment.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Xi Daoyi, a pillar of state under Xue Ju, had fled to Li Gui with three hundred Qiang soldiers. Li Gui had promised him a governorship but never delivered it, and treated him coldly besides. Daoyi burned with resentment.

sentences.zh: 道宜率所部共修仁擊軌，軌敗入城，引兵登陴，冀有外救。

translations.literal: Daoyi led his troops together with Xiuren to strike Gui. Gui was defeated and re-entered the city, leading his troops up onto the battlements, hoping for outside rescue.
translations.idiomatic: Daoyi led his men with An Xiuren against Li Gui. Li Gui was beaten back into the city, climbed the walls with his troops, and waited for outside help that never came.

sentences.zh: 興貴宣言曰：「大唐使我來殺李軌，不從者誅及三族！」

translations.literal: Xinggui proclaimed: "Great Tang sent me to kill Li Gui — whoever does not obey will be punished to the third degree of kin!
translations.idiomatic: Xinggui proclaimed, "Great Tang sent me to kill Li Gui! Whoever does not submit will be executed to the third degree of kin!

sentences.zh: 於是諸城老幼皆出詣修仁。

translations.literal: Thereupon the old and young of all districts came out to seek Xiuren.
translations.idiomatic: At that, the old and young of every district came out to surrender to An Xiuren.

sentences.zh: 軌嘆曰：「人心去矣，天亡我乎！」

translations.literal: Gui sighed: "The people's hearts have left — is Heaven destroying me?
translations.idiomatic: Li Gui sighed, "The people's hearts have left me. Is Heaven destroying me?

sentences.zh: 攜妻子上玉女台，置酒為別，修仁執之以聞。

translations.literal: Taking his wife and children, he ascended the Jade Maiden Platform, set out wine for a farewell, and Xiuren seized him and reported it.
translations.idiomatic: He took his wife and children up to the Jade Maiden Platform, poured a farewell cup of wine, and An Xiuren seized him and sent word of the capture.

sentences.zh: 時鄧曉尚在長安，聞軌敗，舞蹈稱慶。

translations.literal: At the time Deng Xiao was still in Chang'an. When he heard of Gui's defeat, he danced in celebration.
translations.idiomatic: Deng Xiao was still in Chang'an at the time. When he heard that Li Gui had fallen, he danced for joy.

sentences.zh: 高祖數之曰：「汝委質於人，為使來此，聞軌淪陷，曾無蹙容，苟悅朕情，妄為慶躍。

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozu rebuked him: "You submitted your allegiance to another and came here as an envoy. When you heard Gui had fallen, you showed not the slightest troubled countenance — you sought only to please me and recklessly leapt for joy.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozu rebuked him. "You pledged yourself to Li Gui and came here as his envoy. When you heard he had fallen, you did not even look troubled — you danced to please me instead.

sentences.zh: 既不能留心於李軌，何能盡節於朕乎？」

translations.literal: If you could not keep your heart with Li Gui, how can you be fully loyal to me?
translations.idiomatic: If you could not stay loyal to Li Gui, how can you be loyal to me?

sentences.zh: 竟廢而不齒。

translations.literal: In the end he was dismissed and excluded from court.
translations.idiomatic: In the end he was dismissed and never employed again.

sentences.zh: 軌尋伏誅，自起至滅三載，河西悉平。

translations.literal: Gui was soon executed. From his rise to his fall was three years; all of Hexi was pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Li Gui was soon executed. From his rise to his fall took three years, and all of Hexi was pacified.

sentences.zh: 詔授興貴右武候大將軍、上柱國，封涼國公，食實封六百戶，賜帛萬段；

translations.literal: An edict appointed Xinggui General of the Right Martial Guard, Supreme Pillar of State, enfeoffed him as Duke of Liang, granted a fief of six hundred households, and bestowed ten thousand bolts of silk;
translations.idiomatic: An edict appointed An Xinggui General of the Right Martial Guard and Supreme Pillar of State, enfeoffed him as Duke of Liang with a fief of six hundred households, and granted him ten thousand bolts of silk;

sentences.zh: 修仁左武候大將軍，封申國公，並給田宅，食實封六百戶。

translations.literal: Xiuren was made General of the Left Martial Guard and enfeoffed as Duke of Shen; both were given fields and residences, with fiefs of six hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: and made An Xiuren General of the Left Martial Guard and Duke of Shen. Both men received fields and residences, with fiefs of six hundred households each.

sentences.zh: 劉武周

translations.literal: Liu Wuzhou
translations.idiomatic: Liu Wuzhou

sentences.zh: 〈附 苑君璋〉

translations.literal: 〈Appendix: Yuan Junzhang〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈Appendix: Yuan Junzhang〉

sentences.zh: 劉武周，河間景城人。

translations.literal: Liu Wuzhou was a native of Jingcheng in Hejian.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Wuzhou was a native of Jingcheng in Hejian Commandery.

sentences.zh: 父匡，徙家馬邑。

translations.literal: His father Kuang moved the family to Mayi.
translations.idiomatic: His father Liu Kuang moved the family to Mayi.

sentences.zh: 匡嘗與妻趙氏夜坐庭中，忽見一物，狀如雄雞，流光燭地，飛入趙氏懷，振衣無所見，因而有娠，遂生武周。

translations.literal: Kuang once sat with his wife Lady Zhao in the courtyard at night when they suddenly saw something shaped like a rooster, its gleaming light illuminating the ground. It flew into Lady Zhao's bosom; when she shook her clothes, nothing was there. She thereupon became pregnant and bore Wuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: One night Kuang and his wife Lady Zhao were sitting in the courtyard when they saw something shaped like a rooster, its radiance lighting the ground. It flew into Lady Zhao's bosom; when she shook her robes, nothing remained. She conceived and bore Liu Wuzhou.

sentences.zh: 驍勇善射，交通豪俠。

translations.literal: Fierce and brave, skilled at archery; he mingled with bold heroes.
translations.idiomatic: He was fierce and skilled with the bow, and kept company with bold men of the roads.

sentences.zh: 其兄山伯每誡之曰：「汝不擇交遊，終當滅吾族也。」

translations.literal: His elder brother Shanbo often admonished him: "You do not choose your companions — in the end you will destroy our clan.
translations.idiomatic: His elder brother Shanbo often warned him, "You choose your friends without care. One day you will destroy our whole clan.

sentences.zh: 數詈辱之。

translations.literal: He repeatedly scolded and insulted him.
translations.idiomatic: He scolded and humiliated him again and again.

sentences.zh: 武周因去家入洛，為太僕楊義臣帳內，募征遼東，以軍功授建節校尉。

translations.literal: Wuzhou therefore left home for Luoyang, serving in the retinue of Grand Master of Horse Yang Yichen; he was recruited for the Liaodong campaign and for military merit was appointed Establishing-the-Command Pennant Commandant.
translations.idiomatic: Wuzhou left home for Luoyang and entered the service of Grand Master of Horse Yang Yichen. Recruited for the Liaodong campaign, he earned the rank of Establishing-the-Command Pennant Commandant for his military service.

sentences.zh: 還家，為鷹揚府校尉。

translations.literal: Returning home, he became Commandant of the Soaring Hawk Prefectural Guard.
translations.idiomatic: When he returned home he became a commandant in the Soaring Hawk Guard.

sentences.zh: 太守王仁恭以其州里之雄，甚見親遇，每令率虞候屯於閣下。

translations.literal: Prefect Wang Rengong, taking him for a champion of the district, showed him great favor and intimacy, often ordering him to lead military patrols stationed beneath the gate tower.
translations.idiomatic: Prefect Wang Rengong, recognizing him as a local champion, treated him with great favor and often had him lead patrol troops stationed beneath the gate tower.

sentences.zh: 因與仁恭侍兒私通，恐事洩，又見天下已亂，陰懷異計，乃宣言於郡中曰：「今百姓飢餓，死人相枕於野，王府尹閉倉不恤，豈憂百姓之意乎！」

translations.literal: He had an affair with Rengong's serving maid. Fearing the affair would leak, and seeing the realm already in chaos, he secretly harbored a different scheme. He therefore proclaimed in the prefecture: "Now the people starve; the dead lie piled in the fields, yet the prefectural lord closes the granaries without relief — is this the mind of one who cares for the people!
translations.idiomatic: He had an affair with one of Rengong's maids. Fearing exposure, and seeing the empire already in chaos, he began plotting in secret. He spread word through the prefecture: "The people are starving and the dead lie piled in the fields, yet the prefect keeps the granaries shut. Does he care for the people at all?

sentences.zh: 以此激怒眾人，皆發憤怨。

translations.literal: With this he inflamed the crowd; all burned with resentment.
translations.idiomatic: The speech enraged the people, and resentment spread everywhere.

sentences.zh: 武周知眾心搖動，因稱疾不起，鄉閭豪傑多來候問，遂椎牛縱酒大言曰：「盜賊若此，壯士守志，並死溝壑。

translations.literal: Wuzhou knew hearts were wavering, so he feigned illness and did not rise. Many local heroes came to inquire after him. He slaughtered cattle and poured wine freely, saying boldly: "With bandits like this, for a stalwart to keep his integrity means dying together in ditches and gullies.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing that the people's hearts were wavering, Wuzhou feigned illness and stayed abed. Local heroes came to visit him in numbers. He slaughtered an ox, poured wine freely, and declared, "With bandits running wild like this, an honest man who keeps his honor will die in the ditches with the rest.

sentences.zh: 今倉內積粟皆爛，誰能與我取之？」

translations.literal: The grain piled in the granaries is all rotting — who will take it with me?
translations.idiomatic: The grain in the granaries is rotting away. Who will take it with me?

sentences.zh: 諸豪傑皆許諾。

translations.literal: The heroes all pledged themselves.
translations.idiomatic: The heroes all pledged to follow him.

sentences.zh: 與同郡張萬歲等十餘人候仁恭視事，武周上謁，萬歲自後而入，斬仁恭於郡廳，持其首出徇郡中，無敢動者。

translations.literal: With more than ten men of the same prefecture including Zhang Wansui, they waited until Rengong was attending to affairs. Wuzhou paid his respects; Wansui entered from behind and beheaded Rengong in the prefectural hall, carried the head out to display through the prefecture — no one dared stir.
translations.idiomatic: He and more than ten men of the prefecture, including Zhang Wansui, waited until Rengong was holding court. Wuzhou paid his respects while Wansui slipped in from behind and cut Rengong down in the hall. Wansui carried the head through the prefecture as a warning — no one dared move.

sentences.zh: 於是開廩以賑窮乏，馳檄境內，其屬城皆歸之，得兵萬餘人。

translations.literal: They then opened the granaries to relieve the poor, dispatched proclamations throughout the territory; all dependent cities submitted, and he gathered more than ten thousand troops.
translations.idiomatic: They opened the granaries to feed the destitute and sent proclamations across the region. Dependent cities submitted one after another, and Wuzhou raised more than ten thousand troops.

sentences.zh: 武周自稱太守，遣使附於突厥。

translations.literal: Wuzhou styled himself prefect and sent envoys to attach himself to the Turks.
translations.idiomatic: Wuzhou declared himself prefect and sent envoys to submit to the Turks.

sentences.zh: 隋雁門郡丞陳孝意、虎賁將王智辯合兵討之，圍其桑乾鎮。

translations.literal: Sui Assistant Prefect of Yanmen Commandery Chen Xiaoyi and Tiger Guard General Wang Zhibian combined forces to attack him, besieging his Sanggan post.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Xiaoyi, assistant prefect of Yanmen, and Tiger Guard General Wang Zhibian joined forces against him and besieged his post at Sanggan.

sentences.zh: 會突厥大至，與武周共擊智辯，隋師敗績。

translations.literal: The Turks arrived in great numbers; together with Wuzhou they struck Zhibian and the Sui army was routed.
translations.idiomatic: The Turks arrived in force. Together with Wuzhou they struck Zhibian and routed the Sui army.

sentences.zh: 孝意奔還雁門，部人殺之，以城降於武周。

translations.literal: Xiaoyi fled back to Yanmen; his people killed him and surrendered the city to Wuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaoyi fled back to Yanmen, but his own followers killed him and surrendered the city to Wuzhou.

sentences.zh: 於是襲破樓煩郡，進取汾陽宮，獲隋宮人以賂突厥，始畢可汗以馬報之，兵威益振。

translations.literal: He then stormed and took Loufan Commandery, advanced to seize Fenyang Palace, obtained Sui palace women to bribe the Turks. Shibi Khan repaid him with horses, and his military prestige swelled further.
translations.idiomatic: He then stormed Loufan Commandery and seized Fenyang Palace, taking Sui palace women to bribe the Turks. Khan Shibi repaid him with horses, and his military prestige grew ever stronger.

sentences.zh: 及攻陷定襄，復歸於馬邑。

translations.literal: After capturing Dingxiang he returned again to Mayi.
translations.idiomatic: After capturing Dingxiang he returned to Mayi.

sentences.zh: 突厥立武周為定楊可汗，遺以狼頭纛。

translations.literal: The Turks installed Wuzhou as Dingyang Khan and bestowed on him a wolf-head banner.
translations.idiomatic: The Turks installed him as Dingyang Khan and gave him a wolf-head banner.

sentences.zh: 因僭稱皇帝，以妻沮氏為皇后，建元為天興。

translations.literal: He thereupon presumptuously styled himself emperor, made his wife Lady Ju empress, and established the era name Tianxing.
translations.idiomatic: He then declared himself emperor, made his wife Lady Ju empress, and adopted the era name Tianxing.

sentences.zh: 以衛士楊伏念為左僕射，妹婿同縣人苑君璋為內史令。

translations.literal: He made guardsman Yang Fuxian Left Vice-President and his brother-in-law Yuan Junzhang of the same county Inner Secretariat Director.
translations.idiomatic: He appointed guardsman Yang Fuxian as Left Vice-President and his brother-in-law Yuan Junzhang, a man of the same county, as Director of the Inner Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 先是，上谷人宋金剛有眾萬餘人，在易州界為群盜，定州賊帥魏刀兒與相表裡。

translations.literal: Earlier, Song Jingang of Shanggu had more than ten thousand followers, roving as bandits on the border of Yizhou; Dingzhou bandit chieftain Wei Daoer acted with him inside and out.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Song Jingang of Shanggu had more than ten thousand men and roved as a bandit chief on the Yizhou border. Wei Daoer, a rebel leader in Dingzhou, coordinated with him from within and without.

sentences.zh: 後刀兒為竇建德所滅，金剛救之，戰敗，率餘眾四千人奔武周。

translations.literal: Later Daoer was destroyed by Dou Jiande. Jingang went to rescue him, was defeated in battle, and led the remaining four thousand men in flight to Wuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Later Wei Daoer was destroyed by Dou Jiande. Jingang went to his rescue, was defeated, and fled to Wuzhou with four thousand survivors.

sentences.zh: 武周聞金剛善用兵，得之甚喜，號為宋王，委以軍事，中分家產遺之。

translations.literal: Wuzhou heard that Jingang was skilled in using troops; greatly pleased to obtain him, he styled him King of Song, entrusted him with military affairs, and gave him half his household wealth.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing that Jingang was a skilled commander, Wuzhou was delighted. He styled him King of Song, put him in charge of military affairs, and gave him half his household wealth.

sentences.zh: 金剛亦深自結納，遂出其妻，請聘武周之妹。

translations.literal: Jingang also bound himself to him deeply, set aside his own wife, and asked to marry Wuzhou's sister.
translations.idiomatic: Jingang bound himself to Wuzhou in return, set aside his own wife, and asked to marry Wuzhou's sister.

sentences.zh: 又說武周入圖晉陽，南向以爭天下。

translations.literal: He also persuaded Wuzhou to advance upon Jinyang and turn south to contend for the realm.
translations.idiomatic: He also urged Wuzhou to strike at Jinyang and turn south to contest the empire.

sentences.zh: 武周授金剛西南道大行台，令率兵二萬人侵并州，軍黃虵鎮。

translations.literal: Wuzhou appointed Jingang Grand Commissioner of the Southwest Route, ordering him to lead twenty thousand troops to invade Bingzhou, encamping at Huangshe Post.
translations.idiomatic: Wuzhou made Jingang Grand Commissioner of the Southwest Route and ordered him to lead twenty thousand men against Bingzhou, encamping at Huangshe Post.

sentences.zh: 又引突厥之眾，兵鋒甚盛，襲破榆次縣，進陷介州。

translations.literal: He also brought in Turk forces — their military edge was very keen. They stormed and took Yuci County and advanced to capture Jiezhou.
translations.idiomatic: With Turk reinforcements his army's momentum grew fierce. He stormed Yuci County and advanced to take Jiezhou.

sentences.zh: 高祖遣太常少卿李仲文率眾討之，為賊所執，一軍全沒。

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozu dispatched Director of Ceremonial Li Zhongwen to lead troops against him; he was captured by the rebels and the whole army was wiped out.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozu sent Director of Ceremonial Li Zhongwen against him with an army. The rebels captured Zhongwen and wiped out his entire force.

sentences.zh: 仲文後得逃還。

translations.literal: Zhongwen later escaped and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongwen later escaped and made his way back.

sentences.zh: 復遣右僕射裴寂拒之，戰又敗績。

translations.literal: He again sent Right Vice-President Pei Ji to resist; again the battle ended in defeat.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu then sent Right Vice-President Pei Ji to block them, but Pei was defeated again.

sentences.zh: 武周進逼，總管齊王元吉委城遁走，武周遂據太原。

translations.literal: Wuzhou pressed close in his advance. Governor General Prince of Qi Yuan Ji abandoned the city and fled; Wuzhou then seized Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Wuzhou pressed forward. Governor General Prince of Qi Li Yuanji abandoned the city and fled, and Wuzhou took Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 遣金剛進攻晉州，六日，城陷，右驍衛大將軍劉弘基沒於賊。

translations.literal: He sent Jingang to attack Jinzhou; on the sixth day the city fell, and Right Martial Guard General Liu Hongji was lost to the rebels.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Jingang against Jinzhou. On the sixth day the city fell, and Right Martial Guard General Liu Hongji was captured by the rebels.

sentences.zh: 進取澮州，屬縣悉下。

translations.literal: Advancing to take Fenzhou, all subordinate counties submitted.
translations.idiomatic: He advanced on Fenzhou, and all its subordinate counties fell.

sentences.zh: 夏縣人呂崇茂殺縣令，自號魏王，以應賊。

translations.literal: Lü Chongmao of Xia County killed the magistrate, styled himself King of Wei, and responded to the rebels.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Chongmao of Xia County killed the county magistrate, declared himself King of Wei, and joined the rebels.

sentences.zh: 河東賊帥王行本又密與金剛連和，關中大駭。

translations.literal: Hedong bandit chieftain Wang Xingben also secretly joined forces with Jingang; within the Pass there was great alarm.
translations.idiomatic: Hedong rebel leader Wang Xingben also secretly coordinated with Jingang, throwing the Guanzhong region into alarm.

sentences.zh: 高祖命太宗益兵進討，屯於柏壁，相持者久之。

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozu ordered the Prince of Qin to add troops and advance in campaign, encamping at Baiyu — they faced each other for a long time.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozu ordered the Prince of Qin to reinforce his army and advance against them. He encamped at Baiyu, and the two sides faced each other for a long time.

sentences.zh: 又命永安王孝基、陝州總管於筠、工部尚書獨孤懷恩、內史侍郎唐儉進取夏縣，不能克，軍於城南。

translations.literal: He also ordered Prince of Yong'an Xiaoji, Bingzhou Governor General Yu Jun, Minister of Works Du Gu Huaien, and Secretariat Vice-Director Tang Jian to advance and take Xia County but they could not overcome it and encamped south of the city.
translations.idiomatic: He also ordered Prince Yong'an Li Xiaoji, Shaanzhou Governor General Yu Jun, Minister of Works Du Gu Huai'en, and Secretariat Vice-Director Tang Jian to take Xia County. They failed to capture it and encamped south of the city.

sentences.zh: 崇茂與賊將尉遲敬德襲破孝基營，諸軍並陷，四將俱沒。

translations.literal: Chongmao and rebel general Yuchi Jingde stormed and broke Xiaoji's camp; all armies fell together and the four generals were all lost.
translations.idiomatic: Chongmao and rebel general Yuchi Jingde raided Xiaoji's camp and broke it. Every Tang force there collapsed, and all four generals were captured or killed.

sentences.zh: 敬德還澮州，太宗邀擊於美良川，大破之。

translations.literal: Jingde returned to Fenzhou; the Prince of Qin intercepted and struck at Meiliang River and thoroughly defeated him.
translations.idiomatic: Jingde withdrew to Fenzhou. The Prince of Qin intercepted him at Meiliang River and routed his army.

sentences.zh: 敬德與賊將尋相又援王行本於蒲州，太宗復破之於蒲州。

translations.literal: Jingde and rebel general Xun Xiang again went to aid Wang Xingben at Pu Prefecture; the Prince of Qin again defeated them at Pu Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Jingde and rebel general Xun Xiang went to aid Wang Xingben at Pu Prefecture, but the Prince of Qin defeated them there as well.

sentences.zh: 高祖親幸蒲津關，太宗自柏壁輕騎謁高祖於行在所。

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozu personally visited Pu ford; the Prince of Qin rode lightly from Baiyu to pay respects to Gaozu at the temporary court.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozu went in person to Pu Ford. The Prince of Qin rode lightly from Baiyu to meet him at the imperial camp.

sentences.zh: 宋金剛遂圍絳州。

translations.literal: Song Jingang then besieged Jiang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Song Jingang then besieged Jiang Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 及太宗還，金剛懼而引退。

translations.literal: When the Prince of Qin returned, Jingang was afraid and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: When the Prince of Qin returned, Jingang grew fearful and pulled back.

sentences.zh: 武周復攻李仲文於浩州，頻戰皆敗，又饋運不屬，賊眾大餒，於是金剛遂遁。

translations.literal: Wuzhou again attacked Li Zhongwen at Haozhou — repeated battles all ended in defeat, and supply lines failed; the rebel masses grew greatly famished, and Jingang then fled.
translations.idiomatic: Wuzhou again attacked Li Zhongwen at Haozhou, but battle after battle ended in defeat. Supplies ran out, the rebel army grew desperately hungry, and Jingang finally fled.

sentences.zh: 太宗復追及金剛於雀鼠谷，一日八戰，皆破之，俘斬數萬人，獲輜重千餘兩。

translations.literal: The Prince of Qin again pursued and caught up with Jingang at Quezu Valley — in one day eight battles, all victories, capturing and slaying tens of thousands, seizing more than a thousand supply carts.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Qin pursued Jingang to Quezu Valley and fought eight battles in a single day, winning every one. He captured or killed tens of thousands of men and seized more than a thousand supply wagons.

sentences.zh: 金剛走入介州，王師逼之。

translations.literal: Jingang fled into Jie Prefecture; the imperial army pressed upon him.
translations.idiomatic: Jingang retreated into Jie Prefecture, where the imperial army closed in on him.

sentences.zh: 金剛尚有眾二萬，出其西門，背城而陣，太宗與諸將力戰破之，金剛輕騎遁走。

translations.literal: Jingang still had twenty thousand followers; he went out the west gate, formed battle lines with the city at his back, and the Prince of Qin and the generals fought hard and defeated him; Jingang fled away with light cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: Jingang still commanded twenty thousand men. He marched out the west gate and drew up his lines with the city walls at his back. The Prince of Qin and his generals fought fiercely and broke his army, and Jingang escaped with a small cavalry force.

sentences.zh: 其驍將尉遲敬德、尋相、張萬歲收其精兵，舉介州及永安來降。

translations.literal: His fierce generals Yuchi Jingde, Xun Xiang, and Zhang Wansui gathered his elite troops, raised Jie Prefecture and Yong'an, and came to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: His fierce generals Yuchi Jingde, Xun Xiang, and Zhang Wansui rallied his best troops, surrendered Jie Prefecture and Yong'an, and defected to the Tang.

sentences.zh: 武周大懼，率五百騎棄并州北走，自乾燭谷亡奔突厥。

translations.literal: Wuzhou was greatly afraid; leading five hundred cavalry he abandoned Bingzhou and fled north, through Qianzhu Valley escaping to the Turks.
translations.idiomatic: Wuzhou was panic-stricken. He abandoned Bingzhou with five hundred cavalry, fled north through Qianzhu Valley, and sought refuge with the Turks.

sentences.zh: 金剛復收其亡散以拒官軍，人莫之從，與百餘騎復奔突厥。

translations.literal: Jingang again gathered his scattered and fleeing men to resist the government army, but no one followed him; with a little more than a hundred cavalry he again fled to the Turks.
translations.idiomatic: Jingang tried once more to rally his scattered troops to resist the imperial army, but no one would follow. He fled to the Turks again with just over a hundred horsemen.

sentences.zh: 太宗進平并州，悉復故地。

translations.literal: The Prince of Qin advanced and pacified Bingzhou, fully recovering the former territories.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Qin advanced, pacified Bingzhou, and restored all the lost territories.

sentences.zh: 未幾，金剛背突厥而亡，將還上谷，為追騎所獲，腰斬之。

translations.literal: Before long, Jingang turned against the Turks and fled; intending to return to Shanggu, he was captured by pursuers and executed by cutting at the waist.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Jingang abandoned the Turks and fled, intending to return to Shanggu, but pursuing horsemen captured him and cut him in two at the waist.

sentences.zh: 武周又欲謀歸馬邑，事洩，為突厥所殺。

translations.literal: Wuzhou also wished to plot returning to Mayi; the matter leaked out, and he was killed by the Turks.
translations.idiomatic: Wuzhou also plotted to return to Mayi, but when the plan was discovered the Turks killed him.

sentences.zh: 武周自初起至死，凡六載。

translations.literal: From Wuzhou's first rise to his death, in all six years.
translations.idiomatic: From his first rise to his death, Liu Wuzhou's cause had lasted six years.

sentences.zh: 初，武周引兵南侵，苑君璋說曰：「唐主舉一州之兵，定三輔之地，郡縣影附，所向風靡，此固天命，豈曰人謀？

translations.literal: At the beginning, when Wuzhou led troops south to invade, Yuan Junzhang advised him, saying: "The Tang ruler raised the troops of one province, settled the Three Adjuncts, commanderies and counties followed like shadows, wherever he went the wind blew him forward — this is surely Heaven's mandate; how could one call it merely human counsel?
translations.idiomatic: Early on, as Wuzhou led his army south in invasion, Yuan Junzhang urged him: "The Tang ruler mobilized the forces of a single province and secured the Three Adjuncts. Commanderies and counties rallied to him at once; wherever his armies marched, resistance collapsed. That is plainly Heaven's mandate—how could mere human strategy account for it?

sentences.zh: 且并州已南，地形險阻，若懸軍深入，恐後無所繼，不如連和突厥，結援唐朝，南面稱孤，足為上策。」

translations.literal: Moreover, south of Bingzhou the terrain is perilous and obstructed; if an isolated army pushes deep in, I fear there will be nothing to follow behind. Better to join with the Turks, establish ties with the Tang court, and in the south style oneself a separate ruler — that is sufficient as the best plan."
translations.idiomatic: And south of Bingzhou the terrain is rugged and treacherous. If we drive a detached army deep into enemy country, we may find nothing to sustain us. Better to ally with the Turks, maintain ties with the Tang, and hold the south as an independent power. That is the wisest course."

sentences.zh: 武周不聽，遣君璋守朔州，遂侵汾、晉。

translations.literal: Wuzhou did not listen; he sent Junzhang to defend Shuozhou, and then invaded Fen and Jin.
translations.idiomatic: Wuzhou ignored this advice. He left Junzhang to hold Shuozhou and marched into Fen and Jin.

sentences.zh: 及敗，泣謂君璋曰：「恨不用君言，乃至於此！」

translations.literal: When he was defeated, weeping he said to Junzhang: "I regret not taking your words—yet it has come to this!"
translations.idiomatic: After his defeat, he wept and told Junzhang, "I regret not heeding your counsel—and now it has come to this!"

sentences.zh: 武周既死，突厥又以君璋為大行臺，統其餘眾，仍令郁射設督兵助鎮。

translations.literal: After Wuzhou died, the Turks again made Junzhang Grand Secretariat, commanding his remaining forces, and still ordered Yushe to supervise troops to assist in garrisoning.
translations.idiomatic: After Wuzhou's death the Turks made Junzhang Grand Secretariat in chief, put him in command of the remaining forces, and ordered Yushe to bring troops to help garrison the region.

sentences.zh: 高祖遣諭之，君璋部將高滿政謂君璋曰：「夷狄無禮，本非人類，豈可北面事之？

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozu sent envoys to persuade him; Junzhang's subordinate general Gao Manzheng said to Junzhang: "The barbarians are without propriety—they are not of our kind at all. How can one serve them as a vassal facing north?
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozu sent envoys to win him over. Junzhang's subordinate Gao Manzheng told him, "These barbarians know no propriety—they are not men like us. How can we bow north and serve them?

sentences.zh: 不如盡殺突厥以歸唐朝。」

translations.literal: Better to kill all the Turks completely and return to the Tang court."
translations.idiomatic: Better to slaughter every Turk among us and surrender to the Tang."

sentences.zh: 君璋不從，滿政因人心夜逼君璋，君璋亡奔突厥。

translations.literal: Junzhang did not agree; Manzheng, relying on public sentiment, pressed Junzhang by night; Junzhang fled and escaped to the Turks.
translations.idiomatic: Junzhang refused. Manzheng seized on popular discontent and forced Junzhang's hand by night. Junzhang fled to the Turks.

sentences.zh: 滿政遂以城來降，拜朔州總管，封榮國公。

translations.literal: Manzheng then surrendered the city, was appointed Governor General of Shuozhou, and enfeoffed as Duke of Rong.
translations.idiomatic: Manzheng surrendered the city, was appointed Governor General of Shuozhou, and enfeoffed as Duke of Rong.

sentences.zh: 明年，君璋復引突厥來攻馬邑，滿政死之，君璋盡殺其黨而去，退保恆安。

translations.literal: The next year, Junzhang again led the Turks to attack Mayi; Manzheng died in the fighting; Junzhang killed all his faction and departed, withdrawing to defend Heng'an.
translations.idiomatic: The next year Junzhang brought the Turks to attack Mayi again. Manzheng was killed in battle. Junzhang slaughtered his followers and withdrew to hold Heng'an.

sentences.zh: 君璋所部稍稍離散，勢蹙請降，高祖許之，遣使賜以金券。

translations.literal: Junzhang's followers gradually scattered; pressed tight, he requested surrender; Gaozu permitted it and sent envoys granting him an amnesty warrant.
translations.idiomatic: Junzhang's followers gradually melted away. With his position desperate, he asked to surrender. Gaozu accepted and sent envoys bearing a written pardon.

sentences.zh: 會突厥頡利可汗復遣召之，君璋猶豫未決。

translations.literal: Just then Turkic Khan Jieli again sent to summon him; Junzhang hesitated and could not decide.
translations.idiomatic: Just then the Turkic khan Jieli summoned him again, and Junzhang hesitated, unable to decide.

sentences.zh: 其子孝政曰：「劉武周足為殷鑑。

translations.literal: His son Xiaozheng said: "Liu Wuzhou is warning enough.
translations.idiomatic: His son Xiaozheng said, "Liu Wuzhou is warning enough.

sentences.zh: 今既降唐，又歸頡利，取滅之道也。

translations.literal: Now having already surrendered to Tang, yet returning to Jieli — this is the path to destruction.
