translations.idiomatic: Having already surrendered to the Tang, to turn back to Jieli is to choose the road to ruin.

sentences.zh: 糧儲已盡，人情悉離，如更遲留，變生肘腋。」

translations.literal: Grain stores are exhausted, hearts of men all departed; if we delay further, revolt will arise at our elbows and armpits."
translations.idiomatic: Our stores are empty and our men have lost heart. If we linger, treachery will erupt at our very side."

sentences.zh: 恆安人郭子威說君璋曰：「恆安之地，王者舊都，山川形勝，足為險固。

translations.literal: A man of Heng'an, Guo Ziwei, persuaded Junzhang, saying: "The land of Heng'an was an old capital of kings; its mountains and rivers form splendid terrain, sufficient for strong defense.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Ziwei of Heng'an urged Junzhang: "Heng'an was once a royal capital. Its mountains and rivers make it a natural fortress.

sentences.zh: 突厥方強，為我唇齒。

translations.literal: The Turks at this moment are strong—they are our lips and teeth.
translations.idiomatic: The Turks are strong now—they are our vital ally.

sentences.zh: 據此堅城，足觀天下之變，何乃欲降於人也？」

translations.literal: Holding this strong city, one can well observe changes in the realm—why then wish to surrender to other men?"
translations.idiomatic: Hold this stronghold and we can watch how the world turns. Why surrender to another power at all?"

sentences.zh: 君璋然其計，乃執我行人送於突厥，與突厥合軍寇太原之北境。

translations.literal: Junzhang approved his plan; he then seized our traveling envoys and sent them to the Turks, united armies with the Turks, and raided the northern border of Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Junzhang agreed. He seized Tang envoys and handed them over to the Turks, then combined forces with them to raid the northern marches of Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 君璋復見頡利政亂，竟率所部來降，拜安州都督，封芮國公，賜實封五百戶。

translations.literal: Junzhang again saw that Jieli's government was in disorder; in the end he led his followers to surrender, was appointed Governor of Anzhou, enfeoffed as Duke of Rui, and granted a fief of five hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: When Junzhang saw that Jieli's regime had fallen into chaos, he finally surrendered with his followers. He was made Governor of An Prefecture, enfeoffed as Duke of Rui, and granted a fief of five hundred households.

sentences.zh: 高開道

translations.literal: Gao Kaidao
translations.idiomatic: Gao Kaidao

sentences.zh: 三年，復稱燕王，建元，署置百官。

translations.literal: In the third year, he again styled himself King of Yan, established an era name, and appointed all officials.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he again proclaimed himself King of Yan, adopted a reign title, and set up a full court of officials.

sentences.zh: 羅藝在幽州，為竇建德所圍，告急於開道，乃率二千騎援之。

translations.literal: Luo Yi was at Youzhou, besieged by Dou Jiande; he sent urgent appeal to Kaidao, who then led two thousand cavalry to rescue him.
translations.idiomatic: Luo Yi at Youzhou was besieged by Dou Jiande and sent an urgent plea to Kaidao. Kaidao led two thousand horsemen to his relief.

sentences.zh: 建德懼其驍銳，於是引去。

translations.literal: Jiande feared his fierce sharpness, and therefore withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Jiande, fearing his fierce veterans, withdrew.

sentences.zh: 開道因藝遣使來降，詔封北平郡王，賜姓李氏，授蔚州總管。

translations.literal: Kaidao, through Yi, sent envoys to surrender; an edict enfeoffed him as Prince of Beiping Commandery, granted the surname Li, and appointed him Governor General of Yu Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Through Yi, Kaidao sent envoys to surrender. The throne enfeoffed him as Prince of Beiping Commandery, granted him the surname Li, and appointed him Governor General of Yu Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 時幽州大飢，開道許給之粟，藝遣老弱就食，開道皆厚遇之。

translations.literal: At that time Youzhou suffered great famine; Kaidao promised to supply them grain; Yi sent the old and weak to go for food, and Kaidao treated them all generously.
translations.idiomatic: Youzhou was in the grip of famine. Kaidao offered to supply grain, and Yi sent the old and weak to receive it. Kaidao welcomed them all generously.

sentences.zh: 藝甚悅，不以為虞，乃發兵三千人、車數百乘、驢馬千餘匹，請粟於開道。

translations.literal: Yi was very pleased and did not take it as cause for concern; he then sent three thousand troops, several hundred carts, and more than a thousand donkeys and horses to request grain from Kaidao.
translations.idiomatic: Yi was delighted and saw no cause for alarm. He dispatched three thousand soldiers, several hundred wagons, and more than a thousand donkeys and horses to fetch grain from Kaidao.

sentences.zh: 悉留之，北連突厥，告絕於藝，復稱燕國。

translations.literal: Kaidao detained them all, linked north with the Turks, declared rupture with Yi, and again styled himself the Yan state.
translations.idiomatic: Kaidao kept them all, made an alliance with the Turks in the north, broke with Yi, and declared himself King of Yan once more.

sentences.zh: 是歲，劉黑闥入寇山東，開道與之連和，引兵攻易州，不克而退。

translations.literal: That year Liu Heita invaded east of the mountains; Kaidao joined with him, led troops to attack Yi Prefecture, could not overcome it, and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: That year Liu Heita raided the Shandong region. Kaidao allied with him, marched against Yi Prefecture, failed to take it, and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 又遣其將謝稜詐降於藝，請兵援接，藝出兵應之，將至懷戎，稜襲破藝兵。

translations.literal: He again sent his general Xie Leng to feign surrender to Yi, requesting troops for support; Yi sent out troops to respond; as they were about to reach Huairou, Leng suddenly attacked and broke Yi's army.
translations.idiomatic: He sent his general Xie Leng to feign surrender to Yi and request reinforcements. Yi marched out to meet him, but as his force neared Huairou, Leng ambushed and routed it.

sentences.zh: 開道又引突厥頻來為寇，恆、定、幽、易等州皆罹其患。

translations.literal: Kaidao again brought the Turks frequently to raid; Heng, Ding, You, Yi, and other prefectures all suffered their harm.
translations.idiomatic: Kaidao repeatedly led Turkic raids. Heng, Ding, You, Yi, and neighboring prefectures all suffered.

sentences.zh: 突厥頡利可汗攻馬邑，以開道兵善為攻具，引之陷馬邑而去。

translations.literal: Turkic Khan Jieli attacked Mayi; because Kaidao's troops were skilled at making siege equipment, he brought them along, captured Mayi, and departed.
translations.idiomatic: When the Turkic khan Jieli attacked Mayi, he brought Kaidao's men along for their skill at siegecraft. They took Mayi and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 時天下大定，開道欲降，自以數翻復，終恐致罪，又北恃突厥之眾。

translations.literal: At that time the realm was largely settled; Kaidao wished to surrender, but considering how often he had reversed himself, he ultimately feared punishment; moreover to the north he relied on Turkic numbers.
translations.idiomatic: By then the realm was largely pacified. Kaidao wanted to surrender, but having switched sides so often he feared he would be punished. He also counted on Turkic strength in the north.

sentences.zh: 其將士多山東人，思還本士，人心頗離。

translations.literal: His officers and soldiers were mostly men of Shandong; they longed to return to their native soil, and hearts among the men were rather divided.
translations.idiomatic: Most of his officers and soldiers were Shandong men who longed for home, and morale began to fracture.

sentences.zh: 先是，劉黑闥亡將張君立奔於開道，因與其將張金樹潛相結連。

translations.literal: Earlier, Liu Heita's fugitive general Zhang Junli had fled to Kaidao; he thereupon secretly linked up with Kaidao's general Zhang Jinshu.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Liu Heita's fugitive general Zhang Junli had taken refuge with Kaidao and secretly conspired with Kaidao's officer Zhang Jinshu.

sentences.zh: 時開道親兵數百人，皆勇敢士也，號為「義兒」，常在閣內。

translations.literal: At that time Kaidao's personal troops numbered several hundred—all brave warriors, called "foster sons," constantly within the pavilion.
translations.idiomatic: Kaidao kept several hundred personal troops, all fearless fighters known as his "adopted sons," who stayed within his inner quarters.

sentences.zh: 金樹每督兵於閣下。

translations.literal: Jinshu each day drilled troops below the pavilion.
translations.idiomatic: Jinshu drilled his men daily beneath the pavilion.

sentences.zh: 金樹將圍開道，潛令數人入其閣內，與諸義兒陽為遊戲，至日將夕，陰斷其弓弦，又藏其刀，伏聚其槊於床下。

translations.literal: Jinshu was about to besiege Kaidao; secretly he ordered several men to enter the inner pavilion and with the foster sons pretend at games; as evening was near, he secretly cut their bowstrings, hid their sabers, and gathered their spears concealed under the beds.
translations.idiomatic: Preparing to move against Kaidao, Jinshu secretly sent several men into the inner quarters to play with the adopted sons. As evening approached, they quietly cut every bowstring, hid their blades, and stacked their spears under the beds.

sentences.zh: 迨暝，金樹以其徒大呼來攻閣下，向所遣人抱義兒槊一時而出，諸義兒遽將出戰，而弓弦皆絕，刀仗已失。

translations.literal: When darkness fell, Jinshu with his followers shouted loudly and came to attack below the pavilion; the men previously sent, grasping the foster sons' spears, rushed out all at once; the foster sons hastened to go out and fight, but all bowstrings were broken and blades and weapons already lost.
translations.idiomatic: At dusk Jinshu and his men stormed the pavilion with a shout. His agents inside seized the adopted sons' spears and burst out together. The adopted sons rushed to fight, but their bowstrings were cut and their weapons gone.

sentences.zh: 君立於外城舉火相應，表裡驚擾。

translations.literal: Junli in the outer city raised fire in response; inside and outside were alarmed and thrown into disorder.
translations.idiomatic: Junli lit signal fires in the outer city. Chaos erupted inside and out.

sentences.zh: 義兒窮蹙，爭歸金樹。

translations.literal: The foster sons, pressed hard, all turned to Jinshu one after another.
translations.idiomatic: Cornered, the adopted sons turned to Jinshu en masse.

sentences.zh: 開道知不免，於是擐甲持兵坐堂上，與其妻妾樂酣宴。

translations.literal: Kaidao knew he could not escape; he therefore donned armor, held weapons, and sat in the hall, with his wives and concubines drinking and feasting to excess.
translations.idiomatic: Knowing he could not escape, Kaidao donned armor, took up his weapons, and seated himself in the hall to drink and feast with his wives and concubines.

sentences.zh: 金樹之黨憚其勇，不敢逼。

translations.literal: Jinshu's faction feared his courage and did not dare press close.
translations.idiomatic: Jinshu's men feared his fighting spirit and did not dare approach.

sentences.zh: 天將曉，開道先縊其妻妾及諸子而後自殺。

translations.literal: As dawn was near, Kaidao first strangled his wives and concubines and all his sons, then killed himself.
translations.idiomatic: Near dawn Kaidao hanged his wives, concubines, and sons, then killed himself.

sentences.zh: 金樹陳兵，執其義兒，皆斬之。

translations.literal: Jinshu deployed troops, seized the foster sons, and beheaded them all.
translations.idiomatic: Jinshu paraded his troops, seized the adopted sons, and beheaded them all.

sentences.zh: 又殺張君立，死者五百餘人，遂歸國。

translations.literal: He also killed Zhang Junli; more than five hundred died; then he returned to the state.
translations.idiomatic: He also killed Zhang Junli. More than five hundred died in all. Then he submitted to the Tang.

sentences.zh: 開道自初起至滅，凡八歲。

translations.literal: From Kaidao's first rise to his destruction, in all eight years.
translations.idiomatic: From his first rise to his fall, Gao Kaidao's cause lasted eight years.

sentences.zh: 以其地為媯州。

translations.literal: His territory was made Gui Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: His territory was reorganized as Gui Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 劉黑闥

translations.literal: Liu Heita
translations.idiomatic: Liu Heita

sentences.zh: 劉黑闥，貝州漳南人。

translations.literal: Liu Heita was a native of Zhangnan in Beizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Heita was a native of Zhangnan in Bei Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 無賴，嗜酒，好博弈，不治產業，父兄患之。

translations.literal: He was a wastrel, fond of wine, loved gambling, did not manage family property; father and elder brothers were troubled by him.
translations.idiomatic: He was a wastrel who loved wine and gambling and neglected the family estate. His father and elder brothers despaired of him.

sentences.zh: 與竇建德少相友善，家貧，無以自給，建德每資之。

translations.literal: With Dou Jiande from youth he was rather friendly; his family was poor and had no means to support themselves; Jiande often supplied him.
translations.idiomatic: From youth he was on friendly terms with Dou Jiande. His family was poor and could not support him, and Jiande often helped him with money.

sentences.zh: 隋末亡命，從郝孝德為群盜，後歸李密為裨將。

translations.literal: At the end of Sui he became an outlaw, followed Hao Xiaode as a band of brigands, and later joined Li Mi as a lieutenant general.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Sui he turned outlaw, joined Hao Xiaode's band of raiders, and later entered Li Mi's service as a lieutenant.

sentences.zh: 密敗，為王世充所虜。

translations.literal: When Mi was defeated, he was captured by Wang Shichong.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Mi was defeated, Heita was captured by Wang Shichong.

sentences.zh: 世充素聞其勇，以為騎將。

translations.literal: Shichong had long heard of his valor and made him a cavalry general.
translations.idiomatic: Shichong had long heard of his bravery and made him a cavalry commander.

sentences.zh: 見世充所為而竊笑之，乃亡歸建德，建德署為將軍，封漢東郡公，令將奇兵東西掩襲。

translations.literal: Seeing Shichong's actions he secretly laughed at them; he then fled and returned to Jiande; Jiande appointed him general, enfeoffed him as Duke of Handong Commandery, and ordered him to lead elite troops in east-west surprise raids.
translations.idiomatic: He came to scorn Shichong's conduct and secretly mocked it. He fled back to Jiande, who made him a general, enfeoffed him as Duke of Handong Commandery, and put him in charge of raiding parties that struck east and west in surprise.

sentences.zh: 黑闥既遍游諸賊，善觀時變，素驍勇，多奸詐。

translations.literal: Heita had already wandered among all the bandits, skilled at observing changing times, by nature fierce and brave, with much cunning and deceit.
translations.idiomatic: Having served under one rebel lord after another, Heita had learned to read the times. He was naturally fierce and cunning.

sentences.zh: 建德有所經略，必令專知斥候，常間入敵中覘視虛實，或出其不意，乘機奮擊，多所克獲，軍中號為神勇。

translations.literal: Whenever Jiande had some strategic undertaking, he invariably ordered him exclusively to manage reconnaissance; he often secretly entered among the enemy to observe their condition; sometimes taking them unawares, seizing the moment to strike with ferocity, he often overcame and captured much; in the army he was called Spirit-Brave.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever Jiande planned a campaign he put Heita in charge of reconnaissance. Heita often infiltrated enemy lines to probe their strength, then struck without warning and won repeated victories. The army called him Spirit-Brave.

sentences.zh: 及建德敗，黑闥自匿於漳南，杜門不出。

translations.literal: When Jiande was defeated, Heita hid himself at Zhangnan, shut his door and did not go out.
translations.idiomatic: When Jiande was defeated, Heita went into hiding at Zhangnan and refused to leave his home.

sentences.zh: 會高祖征建德故將，范願、董康買、曹湛、高雅賢等將赴長安，願等相與謀曰：「王世充以洛陽降，其下驍將公卿、單雄信之徒皆被夷滅，我輩若至長安，必無保全之理。

translations.literal: It happened that Gaozu was summoning Ji's former generals Fan Yuan, Dong Kangmai, Cao Zhan, Gao Yaxian, and others to proceed to Chang'an; Yuan and the rest consulted together, saying: "Wang Shichong surrendered Luoyang, and under him fierce generals and ministers, Dan Xiongxin and the like, were all exterminated; if we go to Chang'an, there will surely be no way to preserve our lives.
translations.idiomatic: Just then Emperor Gaozu summoned Jiande's former generals—Fan Yuan, Dong Kangmai, Cao Zhan, Gao Yaxian, and others—to Chang'an. They conferenced among themselves: "When Wang Shichong surrendered Luoyang, his bravest commanders and ministers, men like Dan Xiongxin, were all executed. If we go to Chang'an, we will not survive.

sentences.zh: 且夏王往日擒獲淮安王，全其性命，遣送還之。

translations.literal: Moreover, in former days the King of Xia captured Prince Huai'an, preserved his life in full, and sent him back.
translations.idiomatic: And when our King of Xia captured Prince Huai'an, he spared his life and sent him home unharmed.

sentences.zh: 唐家今得夏王，即加殺害，我輩殘命，若不起兵報仇，實亦恥見天下人物。」

translations.literal: The Tang house now having gotten the King of Xia immediately added killing; our remnant lives—if we do not raise troops to avenge, we will truly also be ashamed to face the people under heaven."
translations.idiomatic: Yet the Tang seized our King of Xia and killed him at once. We are men with nothing left to lose. If we do not rise to avenge him, how can we face the world?"

sentences.zh: 於是相率復謀反叛。

translations.literal: Thereupon together they again plotted rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: With that they joined together to plot rebellion once more.

sentences.zh: 卜以劉氏為主吉，共往漳南，見建德故將劉雅告之，且請。

translations.literal: Divination showed that taking one of the Liu clan as leader was auspicious; together they went to Zhangnan, saw Jiande's former general Liu Ya, told him, and made their request.
translations.idiomatic: Divination indicated that a man surnamed Liu should lead them. They went to Zhangnan to see Jiande's former general Liu Ya, told him their plan, and asked him to take command.

sentences.zh: 雅曰：「天下已平，樂在丘園為農夫耳。

translations.literal: Ya said: "The realm is already settled; my pleasure is in hill and garden as a farmer, that is all.
translations.idiomatic: Ya replied, "The realm is at peace. I am content to live as a farmer in the countryside.

sentences.zh: 起兵之事，非所願也。」

translations.literal: Raising troops is not what I wish."
translations.idiomatic: I want no part of rebellion."

sentences.zh: 眾怒，殺雅而去。

translations.literal: The crowd was angered, killed Ya, and departed.
translations.idiomatic: Enraged, they killed him and left.

sentences.zh: 范願曰：「漢東公劉黑闥果敢多奇略，寬仁容眾，恩結於士卒。

translations.literal: Fan Yuan said: "Duke of Handong Liu Heita is resolute and brave with many ingenious stratagems, generous and tolerant of the multitude, with favor bound to the soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Yuan said, "Liu Heita, Duke of Handong, is bold and resourceful, generous with his men, and beloved by the troops.

sentences.zh: 吾久常聞劉氏當有王者，今舉大事，欲收夏王之眾，非其人莫可。」

translations.literal: I have long and constantly heard that the Liu clan should have a king; now in undertaking this great matter, wishing to gather the King of Xia's multitudes—without such a man it cannot be done."
translations.idiomatic: Prophecy has long said a Liu would rule. If we mean to rally the King of Xia's followers, no one else will do."

sentences.zh: 遂往詣黑闥，以告其意。

translations.literal: Thereupon they went to visit Heita and told him their intent.
translations.idiomatic: They went to Heita and laid out their plan.

sentences.zh: 黑闥大悅，殺牛會眾，舉兵得百餘人，襲破漳南縣。

translations.literal: Heita was greatly pleased; he slaughtered an ox to gather the assembly, raised troops numbering a little more than a hundred, and stormed and broke Zhangnan County.
translations.idiomatic: Heita was delighted. He slaughtered an ox to feast his followers, gathered a force of just over a hundred men, and seized Zhangnan County by surprise.

sentences.zh: 貝州刺史戴元詳、魏州刺史權威合兵擊之，並為黑闥所敗，元詳及威皆沒於陣。

translations.literal: Beizhou Governor Dai Yuanxiang and Weizhou Governor Quan Wei combined armies to attack him; both were defeated by Heita; Yuanxiang and Wei both perished in battle.
translations.idiomatic: Bei Prefecture Governor Dai Yuanxiang and Wei Prefecture Governor Quan Wei joined forces against him, but Heita defeated them both. Yuanxiang and Quan Wei were killed in battle.

sentences.zh: 黑闥盡收其器械及餘眾千餘人，於是范願、高雅賢等宿舊左右漸來歸附，眾至二千人。

translations.literal: Heita fully seized their weapons and remaining troops numbering more than a thousand; thereupon Fan Yuan, Gao Yaxian, and other old associates from left and right gradually came to attach themselves; the multitude reached two thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Heita took all their weapons and more than a thousand surviving troops. Fan Yuan, Gao Yaxian, and other old comrades from Jiande's days gradually rallied to him until his force reached two thousand.

sentences.zh: 武德四年七月，設壇於漳南，祭建德，告以舉兵之意，自稱大將軍。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the fourth year of Wude, an altar was set up at Zhangnan; Jiande was sacrificed to; the intent to raise troops was announced; he styled himself Grand General.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of Wude 4 he raised an altar at Zhangnan, offered sacrifices to Jiande, announced his intent to rebel, and proclaimed himself Grand General.

sentences.zh: 淮安王神通、將軍秦武通、王行敏前後討之，皆為所敗。

translations.literal: Prince Huai'an Shitong, General Qin Wutong, and Wang Xingmin one after another campaigned against him; all were defeated by him.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Huai'an Li Shitong, General Qin Wutong, and Wang Xingmin attacked him in turn, and he defeated them all.

sentences.zh: 於是移書趙、魏，其建德將士，往往殺官吏以應。

translations.literal: Thereupon he sent letters to Zhao and Wei; Ji's officers and soldiers often killed officials in response.
translations.idiomatic: He sent messages across Zhao and Wei, and Jiande's former officers and soldiers often killed local officials to join him.

sentences.zh: 黑闥北連懷戎賊帥高開道，兵鋒甚銳，進至宗城，有眾數萬。

translations.literal: Heita linked north with Huairou bandit chieftain Gao Kaidao; his army's edge was very sharp; he advanced to Zongcheng, with followers numbering in the tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: Heita allied with Gao Kaidao, the rebel chief at Huairou. His army swept forward to Zongcheng with tens of thousands of men.

sentences.zh: 黎州總管李世勣不能拒，棄城走保洺州。

translations.literal: Lizhou Governor General Li Shiji could not resist, abandoned the city and fled to hold Ming Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Lizhou Governor General Li Shiji could not hold him off. He abandoned his post and withdrew to Ming Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 黑闥追擊破之，步卒五千人，皆歿於陣，世勣與武通僅以身免。

translations.literal: Heita pursued, attacked, and defeated him; five thousand infantry all perished in battle; Shiji and Wutong barely escaped with their persons alone.
translations.idiomatic: Heita pursued and routed him. Five thousand foot soldiers fell on the field. Li Shiji and Qin Wutong barely escaped with their lives.

sentences.zh: 黑闥又征王琮為中書令，劉斌為中書侍郎，以掌文翰。

translations.literal: Heita further summoned Wang Cong as Secretariat Director, Liu Bin as Secretariat Vice-Director, to manage written documents.
translations.idiomatic: Heita appointed Wang Cong Secretariat Director and Liu Bin Vice-Director to manage his civil administration.

sentences.zh: 遣使北連突厥，頡利可汗遣俟斤宋耶那，率胡騎從之。

translations.literal: He sent envoys north to link with the Turks; Khan Jieli dispatched yabgu Song Yena, leading barbarian cavalry to follow him.
translations.idiomatic: He sent envoys north to treat with the Turks. Khan Jieli dispatched the yabgu Song Yena at the head of Turkic horse to join him.

sentences.zh: 黑闥軍大振，進陷相州。

translations.literal: Heita's army greatly revived; he advanced and captured Xiang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: With his strength renewed, Heita advanced and took Xiang Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 半歲，悉復建德故地。

translations.literal: In half a year he fully recovered Ji's former territories.
translations.idiomatic: Within half a year he had reconquered all of Jiande's former territory.

sentences.zh: 兗州賊帥徐圓朗舉齊、兗之地以附於黑闥，其勢益張。

translations.literal: Yanzhou bandit chieftain Xu Yuanlang raised Qi and Yan lands to attach himself to Heita; his momentum grew ever stronger.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Yuanlang, a rebel leader in Yan Prefecture, brought Qi and Yan under Heita's banner, and Heita's power swelled further.

sentences.zh: 五年正月，黑闥至相州，僭稱漢東王，建元為天造。

translations.literal: In the first month of the fifth year, Heita reached Xiang Prefecture, presumptuously styled himself King of Handong, established the era name as Tiancao.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of Wude 5, Heita reached Xiang Prefecture, declared himself King of Handong, and adopted the era name Tiancao ("Heaven's Creation").

sentences.zh: 以范願為左僕射，董康買為兵部尚書，高雅賢為右領軍，又引建德時文武悉復本位，都於洺州。

translations.literal: He made Fan Yuan Left Vice Director, Dong Kangmai Minister of War, Gao Yaxian Right Army Inspector; he also recalled Ji's former civil and military officials all to their original posts; he made his capital at Ming Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He made Fan Yuan Left Vice Director, Dong Kangmai Minister of War, and Gao Yaxian Right Army Inspector, restored Jiande's former officials to their old ranks, and established his capital at Ming Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 其設法行政，皆師建德而攻戰勇決過之。

translations.literal: His establishing laws and administering government all followed Jiande as model, but in battle he was fierce and resolute beyond him.
translations.idiomatic: He modeled his laws and government on Jiande's, but in combat he was even fiercer and more decisive.

sentences.zh: 於是太宗又自請統兵討之，師次衛州，黑闥數以兵挑戰，輒為官軍所挫。

translations.literal: Thereupon the Prince of Qin again volunteered to command troops to campaign against him; the army halted at Wei Prefecture; Heita repeatedly sent troops to challenge battle, but each time was defeated by the government army.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Qin volunteered to lead the campaign himself. When his army reached Wei Prefecture, Heita repeatedly offered battle, but the imperial forces beat him back each time.

sentences.zh: 黑闥懼，委相州，而退保於列人營。

translations.literal: Heita was afraid; he abandoned Xiang Prefecture and withdrew to hold the Lieren camp.
translations.idiomatic: Heita grew alarmed, gave up Xiang Prefecture, and withdrew to fortify the camp at Lieren.

sentences.zh: 時洺水縣人請為內應，太宗遣總管羅士信入城據守，黑闥又攻陷其城，士信死之，遂據洺州。

translations.literal: At that time men of Ming River County requested to serve as internal collaborators; the Prince of Qin dispatched Governor General Luo Shixin to enter the city and hold it; Heita again stormed and captured the city; Shixin died in the fighting; Heita then held Ming Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Locals in Ming River County offered to act as collaborators inside the city. The Prince of Qin sent Governor General Luo Shixin to hold it, but Heita stormed the city and killed Shixin, then took Ming Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 三月，太宗阻洺水列營以逼之，分遣奇兵，斷其糧道。

translations.literal: In the third month, the Prince of Qin blocked the Ming River and arrayed camps to press upon him, dispatching separately elite troops to cut his grain routes.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month the Prince of Qin camped along the Ming River to hem him in, and sent raiding parties to cut his supply lines.

sentences.zh: 黑闥又數挑戰，太宗堅壁不應，以挫其鋒。

translations.literal: Heita again challenged repeatedly, but Taizong held fast behind walls and would not answer, to blunt their momentum.
translations.idiomatic: Heita provoked battle again and again, but Taizong held his walls and refused to engage, wearing down the rebels' fighting spirit.

sentences.zh: 黑闥城中糧盡，太宗度其必來決戰，預擁洺水上流，謂守堤吏曰：「我擊賊之日，候賊半度而決堰。」

translations.literal: Grain in Heita's city was exhausted; Taizong judged that he would surely come out for a decisive battle, and in advance blocked the upper Ming River, telling the dike guards, "On the day I strike the rebels, wait until they are half across and then break the dam."
translations.idiomatic: When grain in Heita's city ran out, Taizong expected a desperate sortie. He had the upper Ming River dammed in advance and told the dike guards, "On the day we attack, wait until the rebels are half across the river, then break the dam."

sentences.zh: 黑闥果率步騎二萬渡洺水而陣，與官軍大戰，賊眾大潰，水又大至，黑闥眾不得渡，斬首萬餘級，溺死者數千人。

translations.literal: Heita indeed led twenty thousand infantry and cavalry across the Ming to form battle lines; they fought a great battle with the imperial army, the rebels were utterly routed, the floodwaters surged down again, Heita's men could not cross back, more than ten thousand heads were taken, and several thousand drowned.
translations.idiomatic: Heita led twenty thousand foot and horse across the Ming and drew up for battle. The imperial army shattered them, the released flood swept down, and the rebels could not recross. More than ten thousand were beheaded and several thousand drowned.

sentences.zh: 黑闥與范願等以千餘人奔於突厥，山東悉定。

translations.literal: Heita, Fan Yuan, and others fled to the Turks with a little more than a thousand men, and all of Shandong was pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Heita fled to the Turks with Fan Yuan and a little over a thousand followers, and Shandong was fully pacified.

sentences.zh: 太宗遂引軍於河南以討徐圓朗。

translations.literal: Taizong then led his army into Henan to attack Xu Yuanlang.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong then marched into Henan to subdue Xu Yuanlang.

sentences.zh: 六月，黑闥復借兵於突厥，來寇山東。

translations.literal: In the sixth month Heita again borrowed troops from the Turks and came to raid Shandong.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month Heita borrowed Turk troops again and raided Shandong.

sentences.zh: 七月，至定州，其舊將曹湛、董康買先亡在鮮虞，復聚兵以應黑闥。

translations.literal: In the seventh month he reached Dingzhou; his former generals Cao Zhan and Dong Kangmai, who had earlier fled to Xianyu, again gathered troops to join Heita.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month he reached Dingzhou. His former generals Cao Zhan and Dong Kangmai, who had taken refuge in Xianyu, rallied forces to join him.

sentences.zh: 高祖遣淮陽王道玄、原國公史萬寶討之，戰於下博，王師敗績，道玄死於陣，萬寶輕騎逃還。

translations.literal: Gaozu sent Prince Huaiyang Li Daoxuan and Duke of Yuanguo Shi Wanbao against him; they fought at Xiabo, the imperial army was defeated, Daoxuan died in battle, and Wanbao fled back with a few horsemen.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu sent Prince Huaiyang Li Daoxuan and Duke of Yuanguo Shi Wanbao against him. At Xiabo the Tang army was routed; Daoxuan fell in battle and Wanbao escaped with a handful of horsemen.

sentences.zh: 由是河北諸州盡叛，又降於黑闥，旬日間悉復故城，復都洺州。

translations.literal: Because of this all the prefectures of Hebei rebelled and submitted again to Heita; within ten days he recovered all his old cities and re-established his capital at Mingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Every prefecture in Hebei turned rebel and submitted to Heita again. Within ten days he had recovered his old cities and re-established his capital at Mingzhou.

sentences.zh: 十一月，高祖遣齊王元吉擊之，遲留不進。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month Gaozu sent Prince of Qi Li Yuanji to attack him, but Yuanji lingered and would not advance.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month Gaozu sent Prince of Qi Li Yuanji against him, but Yuanji stalled and would not press forward.

sentences.zh: 又令隱太子建成督兵進討，頻戰大捷。

translations.literal: He also ordered the Hidden Crown Prince Chengjian to supervise the advance and attack, winning great victories in repeated battles.
translations.idiomatic: He then put Crown Prince Chengjian in command of the campaign, and the Tang forces won victory after victory.

sentences.zh: 六年二月，又大破之於館陶，黑闥引軍北走。

translations.literal: In the second month of the sixth year he again routed Heita at Guantao, and Heita led his army north in flight.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the sixth year Chengjian routed Heita again at Guantao, and Heita fled north.

sentences.zh: 建成與元吉合千餘騎屯於永濟渠，縱騎擊之，黑闥敗走，命騎將劉弘基追之。

translations.literal: Chengjian and Yuanji joined more than a thousand horsemen and encamped at the Yongji Canal, loosed their cavalry to strike, Heita was defeated and fled, and Chengjian ordered the cavalry general Liu Hongji to pursue.
translations.idiomatic: Chengjian and Yuanji united over a thousand horsemen at the Yongji Canal and unleashed a cavalry charge. Heita broke and ran, and Chengjian sent Liu Hongji in pursuit.

sentences.zh: 黑闥為王師所蹙，不得休息，道遠兵疲，比至饒陽，從者才百餘人，眾皆餒，入城求食。

translations.literal: Heita was harried by the imperial army and could not rest; the road was long and his troops exhausted; by the time he reached Raoyang he had only a little more than a hundred followers left, all starving, and entered the city to seek food.
translations.idiomatic: Harried by the imperial army without rest, his men exhausted by the long flight, Heita reached Raoyang with barely a hundred followers left, all starving, and went into the city to find food.

sentences.zh: 黑闥所署饒州刺史葛德威出門迎拜，延之入城。

translations.literal: Ge Dewei, whom Heita had appointed Prefect of Raoyang, came out to greet and bow, and invited him into the city.
translations.idiomatic: Ge Dewei, Heita's appointed prefect of Raoyang, came out to greet him with bows and invited him into the city.

sentences.zh: 黑闥初不許，德威謬為誠敬，涕泣固請。

translations.literal: At first Heita would not agree; Dewei feigned sincere reverence, weeping and urgently pleading.
translations.idiomatic: Heita refused at first, but Dewei feigned deep devotion, weeping and begging until Heita consented.

sentences.zh: 黑闥乃進，至城傍，德威勒兵執之，送於建成，斬於洺州，山東復定。

translations.literal: Heita then advanced; when he reached the edge of the city Dewei deployed his troops and seized him, sent him to Chengjian, and he was beheaded at Mingzhou; Shandong was pacified again.
translations.idiomatic: Heita advanced to the city wall, where Dewei's troops seized him and sent him to Chengjian. He was beheaded at Mingzhou, and Shandong was pacified once more.

sentences.zh: 徐圓朗

translations.literal: Xu Yuanlang
translations.idiomatic: Xu Yuanlang

sentences.zh: 徐圓朗者，兗州人也。

translations.literal: Xu Yuanlang was a native of Yanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Yuanlang came from Yanzhou.

sentences.zh: 隋末，亡命為群盜，據本郡，縱兵略地，自琅邪巳西，北至東平，盡有之，勝兵二萬餘人。

translations.literal: At the end of Sui he fled into outlawry as a bandit chief, seized his home commandery, and let his troops raid territory; from Langye west to Dongping in the north he held everything, with more than twenty thousand fit for battle.
translations.idiomatic: Late in the Sui he became an outlaw bandit chief, seized his home commandery, and sent raiders across the land from Langye west to Dongping in the north, fielding more than twenty thousand fighting men.

sentences.zh: 初附於李密，密敗，歸王世充。

translations.literal: At first he attached himself to Li Mi; when Mi was defeated he went over to Wang Shicong.
translations.idiomatic: He first served Li Mi; when Mi fell he joined Wang Shicong.

sentences.zh: 及洛陽平，歸國，拜兗州總管，封魯郡公。

translations.literal: When Luoyang was pacified he submitted to the Tang, was appointed Commander-in-Chief of Yanzhou, and enfeoffed as Duke of Lu Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: When Luoyang fell he submitted to the Tang, was made Commander-in-Chief of Yanzhou, and enfeoffed as Duke of Lu.

sentences.zh: 高祖令葛國公盛彥師安輯河南，行至任城。

translations.literal: Gaozu ordered Duke of Geguo Sheng Yanshi to pacify Henan; he reached Rencheng.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu sent Duke of Geguo Sheng Yanshi to pacify Henan, and he reached Rencheng.

sentences.zh: 會劉黑闥作亂，潛結於圓朗，因執彥師舉兵應黑闥，自稱魯王。

translations.literal: Just then Liu Heita rose in rebellion; Yuanlang secretly allied with him, seized Yanshi, raised troops in support of Heita, and styled himself King of Lu.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Heita rebelled, Yuanlang secretly joined him, seized Yanshi, raised troops in Heita's cause, and proclaimed himself King of Lu.

sentences.zh: 黑闥以圓朗為大行台元帥，兗、鄆、陳、杞、伊、洛、曹、戴等八州豪猾，皆殺其長吏以應之。

translations.literal: Heita made Yuanlang commander-in-chief of the great campaign headquarters; powerful ruffians in Yan, Yun, Chen, Qi, Yi, Luo, Cao, and Dai—the eight prefectures—all killed their chief officials to join him.
translations.idiomatic: Heita named Yuanlang commander-in-chief of his great eastern headquarters. Local strongmen across eight prefectures—Yan, Yun, Chen, Qi, Yi, Luo, Cao, and Dai—killed their officials to join the revolt.

sentences.zh: 太宗平黑闥，進師曹州，遣淮安王神通及李世勣攻之。

translations.literal: After Taizong pacified Heita he advanced on Cao Prefecture and sent Prince Huai'an Li Shentong and Li Shiji to attack Yuanlang.
translations.idiomatic: After Taizong crushed Heita he marched on Cao Prefecture and sent Prince Huai'an Li Shentong and Li Shiji against Yuanlang.

sentences.zh: 圓朗數出戰，不利，城內百姓爭逾城降。

translations.literal: Yuanlang sallied out repeatedly but fared ill; the people inside the city scrambled over the walls to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanlang fought repeated sorties without success, while townspeople scrambled over the walls to surrender.

sentences.zh: 圓朗窮蹙，與數騎棄城夜遁，為野人所殺，其地悉平。

translations.literal: Yuanlang, driven to extremity, abandoned the city with a few horsemen and fled by night; country folk killed him, and his territory was wholly pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Cornered, Yuanlang fled the city by night with a few horsemen and was killed by country folk. His territory was fully pacified.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：薛舉父子勇悍絕倫，性皆好殺，仁杲尤甚，無恩眾叛，雖猛何為？

translations.literal: The historiographer says: Xue Ju and his son were matchlessly fierce and valiant, both by nature fond of killing, Rengao especially so; showing no kindness they lost the people's loyalty—what could their ferocity avail?
translations.idiomatic: The historiographer writes: Father and son Xue Ju were ferociously brave beyond compare, both bloodthirsty by nature, Rengao worst of all. Devoid of mercy, they lost the loyalty of their followers—of what use was all that violence?

sentences.zh: 李軌竊據鷹揚，僭號河西，安隋朝官屬，不奪其財；

translations.literal: Li Gui seized the Eagle-Flying post, usurped the title in Hexi, reassured Sui dynasty officials, and did not seize their property;
translations.idiomatic: Li Gui seized power from the Eagle-Flying guard and proclaimed himself in Hexi, reassuring Sui officials and leaving their property untouched;

sentences.zh: 破李贇甲兵，放還其眾，是其興也。

translations.literal: he defeated Li Yun's armored troops and released his men—that was the source of his rise.
translations.idiomatic: he defeated Li Yun's army and sent the captives home—that was how he rose.

sentences.zh: 及殺害謀主，崇信妖巫，眾叛親離，其亡也，宜哉！

translations.literal: But when he killed his chief strategist, trusted sorcerers and shamans, and lost the people and his intimates—his fall was only fitting!
translations.idiomatic: But when he murdered his chief strategist and put his faith in sorcerers, his followers and kin deserted him—small wonder he fell!

sentences.zh: 武周始為鼠竊，偶恣鴟張，不用君璋之謀，竟為突厥所殺。

translations.literal: Wuzhou began as a petty thief, then by chance spread his wings like a fierce owl; he did not heed Junzhang's counsel and in the end was killed by the Turks.
translations.idiomatic: Wuzhou began as a petty bandit and briefly spread his wings; ignoring Junzhang's counsel, he was killed by the Turks in the end.

sentences.zh: 苑君璋及總餘眾，別生異圖，見頡利歸朝，亦是見機者也。

translations.literal: Yuan Junzhang and the remnant host nursed separate designs; when they saw Jieli submit to the court, that too was reading the moment aright.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Junzhang and what remained of the host pursued their own designs; when they saw Jieli submit to the Tang, that too was reading the moment aright.

sentences.zh: 黑闥、開道，勇而無謀，顧其行師，祗是狂賊，皆為麾下所殺，馭眾之道謬哉。

translations.literal: Heita and Kaidao were brave but without strategy; regarded their conduct of armies, they were merely mad brigands, all killed by their own subordinates—how mistaken their way of commanding men!
translations.idiomatic: Heita and Kaidao were bold but lacked strategy; judged by how they led armies, they were mere mad raiders, each killed by his own men—how wrong their way of commanding followers was!

sentences.zh: 贊曰：國無紀綱，盜興草澤。

translations.literal: The encomium says: When the state lacks discipline, bandits rise from the marshes and wilds.
translations.idiomatic: The encomium reads: When the state loses its discipline, brigands rise from the wild margins.

sentences.zh: 不有隋亂，焉知唐德？

translations.literal: Had there been no disorder of Sui, how would the virtue of Tang be known?
translations.idiomatic: Without the chaos of Sui, who would have known the virtue of Tang?
